A flaw was found in libvirt. External inactive snapshots for shut-down VMs are incorrectly created as world-readable, making it possible for unprivileged users to inspect the guest OS contents. This results in an information disclosure vulnerability.

A flaw was found in github.com/go-viper/mapstructure/v2, in the field processing component using mapstructure.WeakDecode. This vulnerability allows information disclosure through detailed error messages that may leak sensitive input values via malformed user-supplied data processed in security-critical contexts.

A flaw was found in GLib. An integer overflow vulnerability in its Unicode case conversion implementation can lead to memory corruption. By processing specially crafted and extremely large Unicode strings, an attacker could trigger an undersized memory allocation, resulting in out-of-bounds writes. This could cause applications utilizing GLib for string conversion to crash or become unstable.

A flaw was found in SoupServer. This HTTP request smuggling vulnerability occurs because SoupServer improperly handles requests that combine Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Connection: keep-alive headers. A remote, unauthenticated client can exploit this by sending specially crafted requests, causing SoupServer to fail to close the connection as required by RFC 9112. This allows the attacker to smuggle additional requests over the persistent connection, leading to unintended request processing and potential denial-of-service (DoS) conditions.

A flaw was found in libsoup, an HTTP client/server library. This HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability arises from non-RFC-compliant parsing in the soup_filter_input_stream_read_line() logic, where libsoup accepts malformed chunk headers, such as lone line feed (LF) characters instead of the required carriage return and line feed (CRLF). A remote attacker can exploit this without authentication or user interaction by sending specially crafted chunked requests. This allows libsoup to parse and process multiple HTTP requests from a single network message, potentially leading to information disclosure.

A flaw was identified in libsoup, a widely used HTTP library in GNOME-based systems. When processing specially crafted HTTP Range headers, the library may improperly validate requested byte ranges. In certain build configurations, this could allow a remote attacker to access portions of server memory beyond the intended response. Exploitation requires a vulnerable configuration and access to a server using the embedded SoupServer component.

A flaw was found in the udisks storage management daemon that allows unprivileged users to back up LUKS encryption headers without authorization. The issue occurs because a privileged D-Bus method responsible for exporting encryption metadata does not perform a policy check. As a result, sensitive cryptographic metadata can be read and written to attacker-controlled locations. This weakens the confidentiality guarantees of encrypted storage volumes.

A flaw was found in libsoup, a library for handling HTTP requests. This vulnerability, known as a Use-After-Free, occurs in the HTTP/2 server implementation. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending specially crafted HTTP/2 requests that cause authentication failures. This can lead to the application attempting to access memory that has already been freed, potentially causing application instability or crashes, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger an application level Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a highly compressed SAMLRequest through the SAML Redirect Binding. The server fails to enforce size limits during DEFLATE decompression, leading to an OutOfMemoryError (OOM) and subsequent process termination. This vulnerability allows an attacker to disrupt the availability of the service.

A flaw was found in polkit. A local user can exploit this by providing a specially crafted, excessively long input to the `polkit-agent-helper-1` setuid binary via standard input (stdin). This unbounded input can lead to an out-of-memory (OOM) condition, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the system.

A flaw was found in p11-kit. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by calling the C_DeriveKey function on a remote token with specific IBM kyber or IBM btc derive mechanism parameters set to NULL. This could lead to the RPC-client attempting to return an uninitialized value, potentially resulting in a NULL dereference or undefined behavior. This issue may cause an application level denial of service or other unpredictable system states.

A flaw was found in libarchive. A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability exists in the ACL parsing logic, specifically within the archive_acl_from_text_nl() function. When processing a malformed ACL string (such as a bare "d" or "default" tag without subsequent fields), the function fails to perform adequate validation before advancing the pointer. An attacker can exploit this by providing a maliciously crafted archive, causing an application utilizing the libarchive API (such as bsdtar) to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in the System Security Services Daemon (SSSD). The pam_passkey_child_read_data() function within the PAM passkey responder fails to properly handle raw bytes received from a pipe. Because the data is treated as a NUL-terminated C string without explicit termination, it results in an out-of-bounds read when processed by functions like snprintf(). A local attacker could potentially trigger this vulnerability by initiating a crafted passkey authentication request, causing the SSSD PAM responder to crash, resulting in a local Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in nano. A local user could exploit a format string vulnerability in the `statusline()` function. By creating a directory with a name containing `printf` specifiers, the application attempts to display this name, leading to a segmentation fault (SEGV). This results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the `nano` application.

A flaw was found in the `readelf` utility of the binutils package. A local attacker could exploit two Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerabilities by providing a specially crafted Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) file. One vulnerability, a resource exhaustion (CWE-400), can lead to an out-of-memory condition. The other, a null pointer dereference (CWE-476), can cause a segmentation fault. Both issues can result in the `readelf` utility becoming unresponsive or crashing, leading to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in libefiboot, a component of efivar. The device path node parser in libefiboot fails to validate that each node's Length field is at least 4 bytes, which is the minimum size for an EFI (Extensible Firmware Interface) device path node header. A local user could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted device path node. This can lead to infinite recursion, causing stack exhaustion and a process crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
The summary service endpoint suffers from an IDOR vulnerability where it fails to verify user ownership of hardware serial numbers, exposing device data to scraping.

Fixed AES-128-CBC keys inside the AcerConnect OTA application let attackers forge authorization credentials for arbitrary IMEI numbers. This allows unauthorized actors to list catalog items and extract protected binaries from pre-signed cloud links.

Multiple out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities were found in GStreamer's pcapparse element. Malformed PCAP records can trigger reads beyond buffer boundaries during IPv4/TCP header parsing. This element is primarily used in debugging pipelines, limiting real-world exposure. A local attacker could trick a user into processing a specially crafted PCAP file, potentially leading to a crash or information disclosure.

A flaw was found in libXpm. A local user with low privileges could exploit an Out-of-Bounds Read vulnerability in the `xpmNextWord()` function by processing a specially crafted or very small XPM (X PixMap) image file. This improper validation of file boundaries can cause an internal pointer to read beyond the file's end, leading to application crashes and Denial of Service conditions.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server in the __aclp__normalize_acltxt() function of aclparse.c. A malformed ACI (Access Control Instruction) string can trigger heap-buffer-overflow writes and reads during ACI parsing. The function fails to validate that the ACI keyword has sufficient length after whitespace stripping, leading to a 1-byte out-of-bounds write and subsequent out-of-bounds reads. An authenticated user with write access to the aci attribute could send a crafted ACI value to silently corrupt heap memory in the directory server process.

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in dnsmasq's find_soa() function in src/rfc1035.c. When parsing NS section records, extract_name() is called with extrabytes=0, failing to validate that 10 additional bytes exist for fixed-length DNS record fields. A remote attacker controlling a DNS zone can exploit this via a crafted NXDOMAIN response to cause a 10-byte heap out-of-bounds read, potentially accessing stale data from prior transactions.

Module: plugins/modules/keyring_info.py 

CVSS 3.1: 5.5 MEDIUM — AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N 

Issue: The module retrieves a passphrase from the OS native keyring (GNOME Keyring, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) and places it directly into result["passphrase"] with no output suppression, no no_log protection, and no documentation warning. 

Root Cause:

Line 105 (protected): keyring_password=dict(type="str", required=True, no_log=True)
Line 127 (NOT protected): result["passphrase"] = passphrase

Observed Output:

{
"changed": false,
"passphrase": "MyMasterP@ssw0rd!SSH_Key_Secret"
}
Visible via register + debug:
{
"keyring_result": {
"changed": false,
"passphrase": "MyMasterP@ssw0rd!SSH_Key_Secret"
}
}

Impact: 

Master passwords, SSH key passphrases and service credentials appear in all Ansible output 

register: keyring_result followed by debug: var=keyring_result prints passphrase in full 

Ansible fact caching backends (Redis, JSON file, memcached) may persist the passphrase 

AWX/Tower job logs silently store the live credential

Fix:

module.exit_json(changed=False, passphrase=passphrase, _ansible_no_log=True)

Also add a documentation warning requiring callers to use no_log: true at the task level.

PoCs


Fig 1: PoC execution showing passphrase in plaintext output


Fig 2: Source code showing no_log=True on input (line 105) vs unprotected output (line 127)
Multiple unbounded alloca() calls in the PulseAudio protocol server.

A heap-buffer-overflow flaw was found in 389 Directory Server (389-ds-base). When
normalizing a Distinguished Name (DN) that contains a legacy-quoted value encoding a
multivalued nested Relative Distinguished Name (RDN), the server can write past the
end of a heap allocation while sorting RDN attribute-value pairs. An unauthenticated
remote attacker can trigger this condition by sending an LDAP operation whose DN
reaches the DN normalization routine, such as a search with a crafted base DN. This
can corrupt heap memory and may cause denial of service.

A denial-of-service and resource exhaustion vulnerability exists within the `GDBus` component of GLib. The `gdbusauth` authentication mechanism fails to enforce proper length limitations on data lines read from a client. An unauthenticated local or remote attacker can exploit this lack of input validation by sending excessively long streams of data, causing the application to consume massive amounts of system memory and CPU, potentially leading to a crash or system hang.

A heap-buffer-overflow flaw was found in Directory Server (389-ds-base). When a DN contains a legacy-quoted value, the server won't close the heap allocation allowing another call to refer to the same memory pointer causing a denial of service or an arbitrary memory write operation.

A flaw was found in gdk-pixbuf. When parsing a specially crafted ICO file with pixel values that exceed the defined palette range, an out-of-bounds read can occur due to improper bounds checking against the actual palette size. This vulnerability causes heap bytes to be interpreted as valid palette indices and rendered as RGB pixel values in the output image, allowing an attacker to extract heap content via the generated output, such as a thumbnail.

An unauthenticated attacker could trigger an Out of Memory condition to crash the Java process for RHCS by repeatedly sending HTTP requests to the TLS endpoint. Depending on how the RHCS server is configured, a manual intervention to restart it may prove necessary.

A flaw was found in libsoup. The chunked transfer encoding parser uses a permissive parsing function for chunk sizes that silently accepts inputs violating RFC 9112, including leading whitespace, plus sign prefixes, and trailing invalid characters. When libsoup operates behind a strict frontend proxy, this parsing differential can be exploited to smuggle HTTP requests.

An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the PCP pmproxy logger servlet using a crafted hostname. This allows arbitrary file and directory creation, potentially leading to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in SSSD. The sss_nss_protocol_parse_addr() function in the NSS responder does not validate the addrlen field against the remaining packet body size. A local attacker can exploit this via a crafted GETHOSTBYADDR request to the NSS responder socket, causing an out-of-bounds read and process crash, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. During SASL PLAIN authentication, the server installs connection-level bind credentials before performing the account-lock check. If the account is subsequently found to be locked, the bind is reported as failed to the client, but the already-installed authenticated state on the connection is not reverted. A client that supplies valid credentials for an account that has been administratively locked can continue to use the same connection with that account's privileges, defeating account lock as an access-revocation control.

A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) bypass vulnerability exists in “stunnel” 5.79 and lower when configured in SOCKS proxy mode. This flaw allows a client to bypass intended localhost restrictions by using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g., “::ffff:127.0.0.1”) or unspecified addresses ("0.0.0.0", "::"), enabling access to loopback-only services on the "stunnel" host that should not be network-reachable.

A flaw was found in SSSD. The extract_authtok_v1() function in the PAM responder does not validate the auth_token_length field against the remaining buffer size before processing. A local attacker can exploit this via a crafted protocol v1 request to the PAM responder socket, causing an out-of-bounds read and process crash, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the RPM Package Manager (RPM). A local user could be affected by a heap buffer overflow vulnerability when processing a specially crafted NDB database file. This issue arises from an error in how RPM handles certain calculations during file parsing, leading to an incorrect memory allocation. An attacker could leverage this to cause a denial of service, making the system unavailable.

A flaw was found in libvirt. During storage volume clone or convert operations, newly created volume images were temporarily world-readable. This was caused by the `qemu-img` utility running with overly permissive file creation settings, allowing any local user to read the full guest disk contents. This vulnerability could lead to sensitive information disclosure from guest virtual machines.

A flaw was found in iperf3. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit a vulnerability in the `JSON_read()` function, which accepts a peer-controlled message length and allocates memory without an upper bound. This allows the attacker to trigger excessive memory consumption, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) through memory exhaustion, severe slowdown, or termination of the iperf3 service.

A flaw was found in the ChunkReader component of the Undertow HTTP server, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to handle chunked transfer encoding. The issue occurs because the parser uses a single internal variable to store both the remaining chunk size and state flags. By sending a specially crafted request with an extremely large chunk size, an attacker can cause these values to overlap, tricking the parser into thinking a request has finished prematurely. This can allow a second, "smuggled" request to be processed out of sync, potentially bypassing security controls.

Multiple Use-After-Free vulnerabilities were found in the add_archive_element function in ld/ldmain.c of the GNU linker (ld), a component of binutils. The root cause is that plugin_maybe_claim() in ld/plugin.c frees the original BFD object via bfd_close/_bfd_delete_bfd when entry->the_bfd->my_archive == NULL, but the caller retains both the original abfd parameter and a shallow copy (orig_input.the_bfd) as dangling pointers. These dangling pointers are subsequently dereferenced at three distinct locations in add_archive_element:

1. Line ~1442: accessing abfd->my_archive via bfd_usrdata(abfd->my_archive)
2. Line ~1493: multiple accesses to abfd and abfd->my_archive in a conditional check and bfd_get_filename call
3. Line ~1525: dereferencing the shallow copy orig_input.the_bfd->my_archive in trace/verbose logging

The vulnerability is triggered when LTO plugins are active (link_info.lto_plugin_active is true) and the input object has abfd->my_archive == NULL, which is a valid state for standalone object files. Red Hat builds binutils with --enable-plugins and --enable-lto, confirming the vulnerable code path is compiled in and reachable.

An attacker who can supply a crafted object or archive file to a build process using LTO-enabled linking could exploit this flaw to cause a denial of service (linker crash via segmentation fault). Arbitrary code execution is theoretically possible through heap manipulation but is substantially mitigated by hardening measures including stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE, ASLR, and PIE.

The attack surface is limited to build-time environments — the linker is a development tool not exposed in production runtime. The most realistic exploitation scenario is a supply chain attack introducing a crafted object file as a build dependency in CI/CD pipelines or development environments.

A flaw was found in libdm. A local attacker could craft a malicious Logical Volume Manager (LVM) metadata configuration with deeply nested structures. This could lead to uncontrolled recursion in the libdm configuration file parser, exhausting the stack and causing any LVM command reading the metadata to crash. This vulnerability results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected systems.

A flaw was found in Undertow, an HTTP server, within its HTTP response header writing path. The `writeString()` method performs a silent narrowing cast from 16-bit Unicode characters to 8-bit bytes when writing HTTP response header values. A remote attacker can exploit this by supplying specific Unicode characters in user-controlled input that an application places into response headers. This can lead to the truncation of these characters into ASCII control characters or special symbols, potentially resulting in limited integrity impact or information disclosure if the application does not properly sanitize user input.

A flaw was found in libsoup's SoupServer HTTP Range header processing. The sort_ranges() comparator in soup-message-headers.c truncates a 64-bit subtraction result to 32-bit int, flipping the sign for range offsets differing by more than INT_MAX. This causes silent omission of requested byte ranges from HTTP 206 Partial Content responses on resources larger than approximately 2 GB.

An algorithmic complexity flaw exists in libsoup's HTTP Range header processing that persists after the CVE-2025-32907 fix.

CVE-2025-32907 addressed memory amplification when a client repeated the same range many times in a single Range header. Commit 9bb92f7a corrected merge correctness in soup_message_headers_get_ranges_internal() in libsoup/soup-message-headers.c, but the coalescing loop still removes merged ranges using g_array_remove_index() for each coalesced element. Because GArray is contiguous, each mid-array removal performs an O(N) memmove. When many identical satisfiable ranges are supplied (for example bytes=0-0 repeated thousands of times), the loop performs O(N²) work coalescing them into a single range.

The vulnerable path is reachable server-side from handle_partial_get() in libsoup/server/http1/soup-server-message-io-http1.c when a SoupServer handler returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty body. No authentication is required. The number of ranges is bounded only by the maximum request header size (~100 KiB), allowing roughly 25,000 ranges per request. Reporter measurements on libsoup HEAD containing the CVE-2025-32907 fix show ~90 ms single-core CPU per such request at the wire maximum, blocking the server's event loop for that duration.

This is a CPU exhaustion / availability issue only. No memory corruption or information disclosure occurs.

Affected: libsoup versions containing the CVE-2025-32907 fix but not merge request !550.
Fixed upstream: MR !550 merged 2026-08-20, replacing per-element removal with O(N) in-place compaction and rejecting Range headers requesting more than 200 ranges.
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsoup/-/issues/538
Related: CVE-2025-32907

A flaw was found in FFmpeg. The tdsc_load_cursor() function writes beyond
the bounds of a heap-allocated buffer when processing crafted TDSC cursor
data. A remote attacker could exploit this by supplying a specially crafted
video file, potentially leading to a denial of service or arbitrary code
execution.

A flaw was found in libsolv, a dependency-resolution library used by RPM-based package managers such as dnf and zypper to work with .solv repository cache files. When libsolv rewrites a .solv cache file, it reads directory-id values from the file's compressed filelist data without validating that they fall within the expected range. A corrupted or specially crafted .solv cache file (for example, one left in a torn state after an unclean system shutdown) can cause an out-of-bounds memory write when a tool such as dnf, yum, or zypper next processes it. Successful exploitation is expected to result in a crash of the affected tool (denial of service); it is not expected to allow arbitrary code execution because the out-of-bounds write always stores a fixed, non-attacker-controlled value.

An unauthenticated client can query the Security Domain hosts inventory via GET /ca/rest/securityDomain/hosts and receive a structured response enumerating internal PKI/CA hosts and roles (security domain topology and participating subsystems), without requiring a principal, client certificate, or session.

A heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability was found in gfs2-utils. The ea_num_ptrs field from on-disk extended attribute metadata is consumed without bounds validation, causing a heap buffer over-read that may disclose sensitive memory contents or cause a crash when processing crafted GFS2 filesystem images.

A flaw was found in GLib2. When g_file_replace() is used with G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION and creating the .goutputstream-XXXXXX temporary file fails, the library unlinks the destination and recreates it without exclusive creation or symlink protection. A local attacker who can write to the destination directory can win that race and redirect the write to another file.

A symlink-following flaw was found in libvirt's qemuTPMEmulatorPrepareHost() function. The function uses a path-based chown() on the swtpm logfile without checking for symbolic links. A local attacker with access to the swtpm account can replace the logfile with a symlink, causing libvirtd (running as root) to transfer ownership of an arbitrary file to the swtpm user.

A flaw was found in SSSD (System Security Services Daemon). A local attacker with privileges to connect to the PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) responder socket can send a specially crafted protocol request. If the `pam_app_services` configuration is enabled and the service item is omitted from the request, a NULL pointer dereference can occur. This vulnerability leads to a denial of service, causing the PAM responder to crash and disrupt authentication services.

A flaw was found in libxml2. A local user or an attacker providing a specially crafted XML catalog can trigger a NULL pointer dereference during XML catalog parsing. This occurs when a `nextCatalog` element lacks its mandatory `catalog` attribute, leading to the application crashing and causing a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 HpackEncoder. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames with a very large MAX_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE. This causes the HpackEncoder to store an excessive number of unique headers, leading to increased CPU usage and memory consumption, ultimately resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A denial of service flaw was found in Poppler's Splash backend. A crafted PDF with tiling-pattern geometry approaching the int32 boundary can cause SplashOutputDev::tilingPatternFill to compute an attacker-controlled repeat count that drives an excessively long loop in the pattern-fill scanline routine, without a corresponding memory allocation. An attacker could exploit this by supplying a malicious PDF to an application that renders it via Poppler's Splash backend, causing the rendering process to consume 100% CPU for an attacker-controlled, extended duration.

A flaw was found in libstoragemgmt. An attacker with control over a local or virtual storage device could provide specially crafted SCSI (Small Computer System Interface) Vital Product Data (VPD) page 0x80 data. This malformed data, specifically an untrusted page length field, can lead to a stack buffer overflow in the `_sg_parse_vpd_80()` function during serial number parsing. Successful exploitation could result in a denial of service by crashing or destabilizing the process querying the serial number.

A flaw was found in SSSD. When configured with the LDAP access provider and `ldap_access_order` including `ppolicy` or `lockout`, a fail-open condition in the LDAP ppolicy access check can occur if a user lookup returns zero results. This can incorrectly return success and cache an allow decision, permitting continued authorization for a deleted or deprovisioned user. A remote attacker with prior valid account context could exploit this to maintain access to information and potentially make limited modifications to resources that should no longer be available.

U-Boot versions 2020.10 before 2026.10-rc4 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in sqfs_read_directory_table() function when allocating the directory table buffer. Attackers can supply a crafted SquashFS image with an attacker-controlled superblock metablks_count value that causes heap buffer under-allocation and out-of-bounds writes, corrupting heap memory and crashing the bootloader.

A flaw was found in SoupServer (libsoup). When an HTTP/1.x client sends a request with Expect: 100-continue and a request body, and SoupServer returns an early final (non-1xx) response before the body is read, the server neither drains the declared body bytes nor closes the connection. On a keep-alive connection, those leftover bytes are interpreted as a subsequent HTTP request. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can place a complete HTTP request in the body and cause SoupServer to process that smuggled request, leading to unintended request handling.

A flaw was found in GEGL. The Radiance HDR loader reads past the end of a memory-mapped image when an uncompressed scanline is shorter than the width declared in the file header. Opening a crafted HDR file crashes the application that uses the loader.

A flaw was found in sssd. This vulnerability allows a local user to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by submitting a specially crafted passkey authentication token that lacks null terminators. The authentication service reads past the end of the provided memory buffer, causing the process to crash and disrupting authentication services.

A flaw was found in SSSD. In configurations where the autofs responder service is enabled, memory allocated during successful request processing is not released until the client connection terminates. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability by maintaining an open connection and repeatedly submitting valid requests, leading to memory exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in SSSD. An unprivileged local user can repeatedly request master automount map updates through the autofs responder due to missing authorization checks. This triggers global cache invalidation and forces repeated lookups to backend directory providers, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) from degraded automount availability and elevated resource consumption.

A flaw was found in SSSD. When configured to enforce account expiration using LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) shadow attributes, SSSD fails to treat an expiration value of zero as an expired account. A user with valid credentials for an expired account can exploit this flaw to bypass access controls and authenticate to the system. This allows unauthorized access to persist after the account was intended to be deactivated.

A flaw was found in SSSD. An issue in the Kerberos Credential Manager (KCM) responder allows a local user to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by maintaining a persistent connection and repeatedly storing and destroying credentials. Because the service fails to release cached objects from memory when credentials are removed, memory consumption grows continuously, ultimately exhausting available memory and rendering the service unresponsive.

A flaw was found in SSSD. A local attacker can exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted request with an invalid packet length to the autofs responder UNIX socket. This causes an integer underflow and an out-of-bounds memory read, which can crash the responder process and result in a denial of service (DoS).

A flaw was found in SSSD. An unprivileged local user can repeatedly request lookups for nonexistent entries through the Name Service Switch (NSS) responder. Because the negative cache does not limit the total number of stored entries and only removes expired records when an existing key is rechecked, the cache can grow without bound. This behavior can lead to memory exhaustion, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) as the responder becomes unresponsive or terminates.

A flaw was found in sssd. A local attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a crafted Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) request containing a zero-length authentication token to the responder socket. Due to missing input validation, the service attempts to read beyond buffer boundaries when processing the token, causing the PAM responder to crash.

A flaw was found in SSSD. A local attacker with access to the Name Service Switch (NSS) responder UNIX socket can trigger an integer underflow by sending a specially crafted request with an undersized packet header. This issue causes an out-of-bounds memory read during packet parsing, crashing the responder process and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in SSSD. When configured to use Microsoft Entra ID, search inputs are not properly sanitized before being incorporated into directory query filters. A local user can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted lookup request, manipulating the query logic to cause unauthorized information disclosure from the directory.

A flaw was found in `sssd-kcm`. A local user or process able to connect to the `sssd-kcm` UNIX socket can exploit this vulnerability. By sending a large request length header and then stalling the connection, an attacker can cause the system to preallocate significant memory. This leads to memory exhaustion within the `sssd-kcm` responder, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected deployments.

A flaw was found in GIMP’s X cursor (XMC) thumbnail loader. When GIMP generates a thumbnail for a crafted XMC file, it allocates a pixel buffer using a width * height size computed in 32-bit signed arithmetic. If that product overflows, the allocation is smaller than the true image extent. A subsequent GEGL buffer read uses the unwrapped dimensions and performs an out-of-bounds read on the heap, after integer overflow in the size calculation. This can crash GIMP or corrupt process memory.

A flaw was found in libhangul. When parsing Hanja dictionary files, the library fails to verify that an entry contains a valid value alongside its key. By providing a specially crafted dictionary file to an application that queries it, an attacker can trigger an unexpected application crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in GIMP. The XCF loader processes image-simulation-intent and image-simulation-bpc parasites without ensuring the parasite data is present before dereferencing it. Opening a specially crafted XCF file with a zero-size simulation parasite can cause a NULL pointer dereference and crash the GIMP application.

A flaw was found in openstack-network-exporter. The HTTP server within the component is configured without essential timeout settings, such as ReadHeaderTimeout. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to initiate multiple slow HTTP header connections. By trickling header bytes, the attacker can exhaust server resources, specifically file descriptors, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) that prevents legitimate Prometheus metric scraping and alerting.

A flaw was found in BlueZ. An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the btmon Bluetooth monitor tool when processing crafted HCI Return Link Keys events. A maliciously crafted btsnoop capture file can specify a large number of link keys that exceeds the actual packet data, causing btmon to read beyond the allocated buffer and crash.

A flaw was found in the clevis PKCS#11 pin. The clevis-pkcs11-afunix-socket-unlock daemon logs LUKS disk encryption passphrases in plaintext to a log file. The log file is created without restrictive permissions, making it world-readable under the default process umask. A local attacker can read the log file to obtain the LUKS passphrase.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP BookIt bookit allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.

This issue affects BookIt: from n/a through 2.6.0.5.

A flaw was found in nfs-utils. The fsidd daemon improperly handles input received over its local domain socket by relying on program assertions to verify command arguments. A local user can exploit this vulnerability by sending a malformed request lacking the required arguments to trigger an assertion failure. This causes the daemon to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for filesystem identifier lookup services until restarted.

A flaw was found in libtirpc. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted PMAPPROC_DUMP replies to a client application that uses the pmap_getmaps() function against an attacker-controlled host. This unbounded decoding can lead to excessive memory and CPU allocation, causing the client process to experience a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.

A flaw was found in parted. A heap-based buffer overflow exists in libparted's file system resizing logic when handling FAT16 volumes. By convincing a user or administrator to resize a specially crafted FAT16 file system image with malformed directory metadata, an attacker can trigger an oversized read into a fixed-size memory buffer. This issue causes memory corruption, resulting in an application crash and a denial of service (DoS).

A flaw was found in GIMP. Importing a crafted SBZ palette without a color-model attribute can cause a NULL pointer dereference during string comparison, resulting in denial of service of the GIMP application.

A flaw was found in GNU patch. An attacker can achieve arbitrary file creation outside the intended working directory by enticing a user or automated workflow to apply a specially crafted patch file. Due to missing validation during automatic patch reversal, absolute file paths in patch headers are accepted rather than rejected. Consequently, the utility can create files in arbitrary locations with the permissions of the executing user.

A flaw was found in FreeIPA. An improper authorization check allows an authenticated host to retrieve and revoke digital certificates assigned to other users or services. This issue occurs because FreeIPA verifies ownership solely by matching the host name to the certificate's subject Common Name (CN), without confirming actual ownership in the directory service. Consequently, an enrolled host can disrupt services by revoking certificates belonging to other entities.

A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability was found in gssproxy. When a GSSX_INIT_SEC_CONTEXT request is received with the target_name field absent, the daemon dereferences the resulting NULL pointer and crashes. The request requires no authentication, allowing any local user to crash the gssproxy daemon via its Unix socket. The daemon does not automatically restart, resulting in a persistent denial of service that also affects dependent services such as Kerberized NFS and IdM.

Dell PowerProtect Data Domain, Feature Release versions 7.7.1.0 through 8.8, LTS2024 release versions 7.13.1.0 through 7.13.1.80, LTS2025 release versions 8.3.1.0 through 8.3.1.40, LTS2026 release versions 8.6.1.0 through 8.6.1.20, contain an Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Filesystem access for attacker.

Dell PowerProtect Data Domain, Feature Release versions 7.7.1.0 through 8.8, LTS2024 release versions 7.13.1.0 through 7.13.1.80, LTS2025 release versions 8.3.1.0 through 8.3.1.40, LTS2026 release versions 8.6.1.0 through 8.6.1.20, contain an Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The TCP DNS service uses a small fixed pool of child processes and does not set a receive timeout on client connections. A remote attacker can open idle TCP connections to port 53 and occupy the entire pool, preventing new TCP DNS connections and DNSSEC validation that requires TCP fallback. UDP DNS resolution continues, and occupied slots are released after a fixed lifetime.

A flaw was found in dnsmasq. After a reduction of internal domain-name buffer sizes, the DNSSEC validator can write a few bytes past a name buffer when converting names to and from DNS wire format. An attacker who can cause the server to validate a crafted DNSSEC response may overwrite a small amount of adjacent heap metadata. DNSSEC support is not compiled in by default and must also be enabled at runtime.

In Modem, there is a possible out of bounds write due to an incorrect bounds check. This could lead to remote denial of service, if a UE has connected to a rogue base station controlled by the attacker, with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation. Patch ID: MOLY01777997; Issue ID: MSV-8905.

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-good (avidemux). In the subindex parser, missing validation of the entry count can cause excessive memory allocation and denial of service. Because avidemux is auto-plugged by playbin, decodebin, and gst-discoverer, opening or previewing a crafted AVI is sufficient to trigger the issue. Fixed upstream in gst-plugins-good 1.28.6 (GStreamer-SA-2026-0072).

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its SMART on FHIR implementation because checkUserHasAccessToPatient() in BearerTokenAuthorizationStrategy.php unconditionally returns true. Authenticated users or malicious SMART apps can manipulate token launch context to bind requests to arbitrary patient UUIDs, gaining unauthorized read/write access to other patients' FHIR resources.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in interface/forms/eye_mag/report.php that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by adding unescaped document notes. Attackers with document-note write access can store malicious JavaScript in a retina document note that executes when clinicians generate the Eye Exam patient report, exposing session cookies.

The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later do not free partially decoded buffers on failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS messages.

krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly trigger key decryption failures.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good MOV/MP4 demuxer. When processing an uncompressed video track, qtdemux fails to validate the declared row alignment and chroma geometry before using them to build a video buffer layout. A crafted file can cause an out-of-bounds heap read while the sample is copied, potentially crashing the application and causing denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Bink video decoder because decode_frame() in libavcodec/bink.c ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers can supply a crafted Bink file with a frame of about 2^28 bytes, overflowing the bit count and crashing the process for denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in tqi_decode_frame() in libavcodec/eatqi.c, which ignores init_get_bits() failure after an integer overflow. Attackers can supply a crafted EA file with a pIQT chunk carrying a 2^28-byte payload to crash the process, causing denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in bit_allocation() in libavcodec/imc.c that allows attackers to hang decoding by supplying audio blocks with a negative bit budget. Attackers can craft IMC or IAC audio files that drive freebits negative, causing the reduction loop to never terminate and consuming 100% CPU.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in ape_decode_frame() in libavcodec/apedec.c that fails to enforce the 73728-sample limit for legacy APE frames. Attackers can supply a crafted legacy Monkey's Audio file declaring an enormous nblocks value to force gigabyte-scale allocations and cause denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in libxevd_receive_frame() in libavcodec/libxevd.c that fails to free pkt_au when an access unit produces no picture. Attackers can supply a crafted EVC stream with many access units containing only parameter sets or non-frame NAL units to exhaust memory in the decoding application.

FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in ff_hap_set_chunk_count() in libavcodec/hap.c, where a shadowed return variable masks reallocation failures. Attackers can supply a crafted Hap video frame with an oversized chunk count so the decoder writes through a NULL chunk table, crashing the application.

FFmpeg 8.1 through 9.0.2 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the libavcodec/exif.c parser that allows attackers to amplify allocations by pointing many IFD entries at overlapping payloads. Attackers can embed a small crafted EXIF block in TIFF, JPEG, PNG or WebP images to trigger quadratic memory allocation, causing denial of service in decoding applications.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in pps_3d_extension() in libavcodec/hevc/ps.c that allows attackers to exhaust CPU through unbounded depth lookup table loops. Attackers can supply crafted HEVC files with repeated PPS NAL units that trigger hundreds of millions of bit skips, stalling decoders, parsers, and ffprobe.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a division by zero vulnerability in ff_aom_parse_film_grain_sets() that fails to reject AFGS1 scaling points with repeated x values. Attackers can supply crafted HEVC or VVC files with zero-increment scaling points in T.35 SEI messages, causing generate_scaling() to divide by zero and crash the decoder.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a reachable assertion vulnerability in the TTA encoder's tta_encode_frame() in libavcodec/ttaenc.c, which never reserves output packet space for the 4-byte CRC. Attackers can supply audio whose sample values and length produce a small, poorly compressible final frame, triggering the av_assert0() in flush_put_bits() and aborting applications transcoding to TTA.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in pcm_dvd_encode_frame() in libavcodec/pcm-dvdenc.c when a 24-bit final frame holds fewer samples than one block. Attackers can supply 24-bit 48 or 96 kHz audio whose length leaves a short final frame, causing the loop counter to wrap and crash the transcoding process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in parse_frame_header() in libavcodec/jpegxl_parser.c that fails to validate TOC entry counts against remaining input. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XL frame header with a permuted TOC and huge toc_count, making the parser loop excessively and exhaust CPU.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in libavcodec/nvdec.c because ff_nvdec_start_frame() fails to reset ctx->bitstream after slice errors. Attackers can supply crafted video that abandons a picture before end_frame, causing cuvidDecodePicture() to read freed heap memory, crashing applications or exposing stale heap contents.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in v4l2_buffer_swframe_to_buf() in libavcodec/v4l2_buffers.c that mishandles frames with negative linesize. Attackers can supply bottom-up AVI or PNM/PFM files that are transcoded to a V4L2 M2M encoder, crashing the application or leaking heap memory into encoded output.
Out-of-bounds read in Microsoft Remote Registry Service allows an authorized attacker to deny service over a network.
Server-side request forgery (ssrf) in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
Untrusted pointer dereference in Windows Link-Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over an adjacent network.
Buffer over-read in Windows Active Directory Certificate Services allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

A flaw was found in cpio. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering a stack-based buffer overflow when creating archives in tar or ustar formats. When archiving files owned by users or groups with names exceeding 32 characters, cpio copies these names into fixed-size memory without verifying their length. This unbounded copy corrupts stack memory and causes the application to crash.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder on builds with the JSON PAM extension enabled. A local attacker can submit a crafted authentication request containing a non-string OAuth2 code value. Missing JSON type validation leads to a NULL pointer dereference, terminating the PAM responder and disrupting SSSD-backed authentication.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder. A local attacker can send an authentication request without first negotiating the client protocol version. The responder dereferences a NULL protocol-version pointer and crashes, disrupting SSSD-backed authentication. Repeated crafted requests can sustain the denial of service.

Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. The DELETE /share/right/ endpoint checks for a membership matching the target group, the authenticated user, and share_admin=True, but omits accepted=True. An authenticated remote attacker who has been invited to a group with share-admin privileges, and who knows a group share-right UUID, can therefore delete that group's share-right record without accepting the invitation or after declining it. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. Deletion revokes the group's access to the affected share and its contained secrets for all accepted group members, without deleting the underlying data or disclosing secret contents. The issue was fixed in version 7.5.1 of both editions, released on 2026-10-13.

MRBS before 1.13.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject spreadsheet formulas because the escape() function in web/report.php fails to neutralize leading formula characters. Attackers can store formulas in booking names, descriptions or custom fields that execute when privileged users open exported CSV reports, enabling data exfiltration or command execution via DDE.

paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in image upload because ImageServiceImpl.validateStaticImg accepts SVG files, which are then served from the site origin when local storage is used. Authenticated attackers can upload script-bearing SVG images that execute when victims view them, stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie to hijack accounts.

paicoding commit 766c48b through commit 903adce contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in payment notifications, where NotifyMsgListener inserts the payer's display name unescaped and notify-system-item.html renders it via th:utext. Authenticated attackers can set a malicious display name and start a pending payment on a paid article, executing script in the author's browser when the author views notifications.

paicoding 1.0.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to unlock paid articles by guessing weak payment confirmation codes. Attackers can start a payment, enumerate roughly 2000 IdUtil.genPayCode counter values, and submit the matching verifyCode to the unauthenticated callback to mark it paid.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.11.3 contains a broken access control vulnerability in which the isAutor() function in MdlObject.php grants accessRight=3 based solely on object authorship without verifying the user still belongs to the object's space. Attackers who were previously members and authored objects can retain unauthorized read access to space objects even after being removed from the space, leading to persistent information disclosure.

A flaw was found in D-Bus. In configurations where the daemon falls back to using the Unix select() mechanism for event monitoring, it does not verify whether file descriptor numbers exceed allocated limits. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by opening a large number of concurrent connections to trigger an out-of-bounds write on the stack. This can cause the daemon to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

Pulse from 5.0.17 before 6.8.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/ai/approvals endpoints that allows authenticated viewer-level users to manage approval requests. Attackers can list pending requests to expose proposed commands and targets, and approve or deny other users' requests, altering decision and audit state.

littlefs through 2.11.3, when built with LFS_MIGRATE, contains a type confusion vulnerability in lfs_dir_traverse() that treats a stack lfs_diskoff struct as an lfs_attr array. Attackers can supply a crafted littlefs v1 image whose metadata is read as LFS_FROM_USERATTRS during migration, causing out-of-bounds stack reads and process crashes.

Improper restriction of intended endpoints in the connection configuration handling of the AWS Labs Timestream for InfluxDB MCP Server (awslabs.timestream-for-influxdb-mcp-server) before 0.0.19 might allow a remote unauthenticated actor (via prompt injection) to obtain the InfluxDB API token configured on the server, sent to a crafted endpoint controlled through an InfluxDB URL introduced in the MCP client context.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.0.19 or later and rotate any InfluxDB API tokens configured for the server.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in get_scalar_api_reference() that embeds unescaped OpenAPI content inside an inline script element. Attackers can supply an OpenAPI document containing a </script><script> sequence in content or sources to execute scripts in the documentation origin for every user viewing the API reference.

A maliciously crafted DWG or DXF file containing a crafted field format string, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force an Out-of-Bounds Read vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to read sensitive data from process memory.

A maliciously crafted DXF file containing crafted VBA project data, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force an Out-of-Bounds Read vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to read sensitive data from process memory.

Kadence Security plugin for WordPress (better-wp-security) before 10.0.6.1 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade per-host login lockouts by exploiting IPv6 address handling in ITSEC_Lib::get_ip(), which keys failed-login counters on the full 128-bit IPv6 address rather than a /64 prefix. Attackers who control a routed IPv6 /64 can send each login attempt from a new address within that prefix, resetting the per-host counter each time to perform password spraying and username enumeration, and can similarly evade the auto_ban_admin immediate ban via address rotation.

Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b contains an integer underflow in plm_demux_seek() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via crafted MPEG-PS files. Attackers can supply a PES packet with payload under 6 bytes, wrapping the packet->length - 6 loop bound during force_intra seeking to crash applications.

AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the TextareaAutosize component that allows workspace members with edit access to inject markup by copying unescaped values into a hidden mirror via innerHTML. Attackers can store a database row title or checklist task containing an element with an event handler to execute script in browsers of users opening the row, including unauthenticated published page visitors.

Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.

wireguard_webadmin before 0.9981 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in scheduler/views.py that allows low-privilege authenticated users to manage peer schedules without Peer Manager level. View Only or Debugging Analyst users can create, modify, and delete schedule profiles and time slots to disable WireGuard peers or keep disabled peers off.

UI misrepresentation in SVG in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker leveraging social engineering to spoof UI elements via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)
UI misrepresentation in UI in Google Chrome on on Android prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker to spoof address bar via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Low)

Poppler through 26.11.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in NSSCryptoSignBackend.cc that allows attackers to trigger reads of freed CMS arena memory during repeated signature verification. Attackers can supply a signed PDF embedding the signer certificate to crash applications or pdfsig runs validating multiple signatures, or cause incorrect certificate validation results.

Pleasanter contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Publishing feature. If this vulnerability is exploited, a remote unauthenticated attacker who can access a site published using the product may obtain, by sending a specially crafted request, information on records of unpublished sites (e.g., titles), as well as the names of users, groups, and organizations registered in the same tenant. Note that the vulnerability only affects configurations where both of the following conditions are met: a site is published using the Publishing feature, and the published site contains link items (items linked to other sites, users, groups, or organizations).

Gargoyle 2023.1 through 2026.1.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the bundled Plus interpreter's ReadString() function in terps/plus/loaddatabase.c that fails to handle end of file. Attackers can supply an empty, truncated, or crafted .plus game file that hangs Gargoyle at full CPU until the user kills it.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the BGR, CMYK, GRAY, RGB, YCBCR and YUV decoders that allows attackers to crash the application. Attackers can supply a crafted image to these decoders to trigger a crash and disrupt image processing services.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in various coders that allows attackers to allocate excessive memory by supplying images with many profiles. Attackers can craft images containing a high number of embedded profiles to exhaust memory and cause denial of service, bypassing security policy limits.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in the ASE decoder caused by a missing security policy check. Attackers can supply crafted ASE files that evade configured resource policies to cause excessive memory usage and denial of service.

Dell PowerStore contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. A low-privileged authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to execution of malicious script in a higher-privileged user's session.

A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing authentication requests using the Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes the server process to crash before validating authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).
An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the PHP session management mechanism

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the ngx_stream_ssl_module module with dynamic certificate loading and the ngx_stream_proxy_module module with the proxy_protocol v2 directive, an abbreviated SSL handshake can cause a worker process to terminate.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. This is a data plane vulnerability only; there is no control plane exposure.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When a task or its parameters are marked no_log: true, sensitive values passed to a module's warn() or deprecate() calls are not redacted and are printed in cleartext to stdout/stderr in warning and deprecation messages. The 'warnings' and 'deprecations' keys are retained in the PRESERVE allow-list in lib/ansible/_internal/_task.py when the task result is censored, so sensitive parameters bypass masking and can be disclosed in output captured in terminal sessions, CI logs, and any automation wrapping ansible-playbook, even though every task touching the secrets is marked no_log: true.

OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-uhttpd before commit d38658bedbdd811b798da16b49301478c6cf21af grants '/*' file read in its rpcd read ACL, which rpcd's fnmatch matching applies to every path. Users delegated only luci-app-uhttpd read access can read any file as root, including /etc/shadow, /etc/config/* credentials, /etc/uhttpd.key, and /etc/dropbear keys.

The rsyslog's`imuxsock` special parser can end up writing into the received message raw buffer when trying to replace the message timestamp with the system's timestamp. A local attacker with the ability to write to the `imuxsock` socket can leverage that by crafting a malformed PRI value with a short timestamp to lead the rsyslog to perform the out-of-bounds write.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_node_end() that allows attackers to crash the application through an unmatched closing ProtoDeclare element. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file with a mismatched closing ProtoDeclare or ExternProtoDeclare element, causing a dereference of a NULL parsing_proto pointer and denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a divide by zero vulnerability in DumpTrackInfo() in applications/mp4box/filedump.c that fails to check the media timescale for zero. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with a zero media timescale to make MP4Box -infon raise SIGFPE and crash, causing denial of service.

A cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in Win Bird JYUGYO SHIEN browser extensions for Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge, which allows an attacker to execute arbitrary script in the user's web browser.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the npm connection health report was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the Triggers page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the Build Features page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the artifact dependency tree was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the diff view page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the checkout rules path preview was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in build statistics charts was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the Large Build Log health report was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the project Report Tab dialog was possible

A maliciously crafted SBSAR file, when imported or loaded through the Substance in 3ds Max plugin in Autodesk 3ds Max, can trigger an Out-of-Bounds Read (unvalidated element begin-pointer) vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause an application crash or potentially read sensitive data from the current process.

A maliciously crafted SBSAR file, when imported or loaded through the Substance in 3ds Max plugin in Autodesk 3ds Max, can trigger an Out-of-Bounds Read (table-index lookup) vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause an application crash or potentially read sensitive data from the current process.

A maliciously crafted SBSAR file, when imported or loaded through the Substance in 3ds Max plugin in Autodesk 3ds Max, can trigger a Stack Overflow vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause an application crash.

OFFIS DCMTK 3.5.4 through 3.7.1 contains an integer overflow in DJCodecEncoder::encodeTrueLossless size checks that allows attackers to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read. Attackers can supply a crafted DICOM file with large Columns, Rows and SamplesPerPixel values that, when compressed with true-lossless JPEG, crashes the application.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 3.7.0 before 3.30.5 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in parseAttributes and parseShortcodeAttributes that allows attackers to exhaust CPU through quadratic backtracking. Attackers can supply Markdown with long crafted attribute strings parsed by createBlockMarkdownSpec, createAtomBlockMarkdownSpec or createInlineMarkdownSpec to stall browser pages or server processes.
In JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.11.1 files outside the project could be overwritten via shell output redirection

littlefs 2.8.0 through 2.11.3 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in lfs_mount_() that allows attackers to crash processes mounting crafted filesystem images when block_count is 0. Attackers can supply an image lacking a superblock entry or recording block_count 0, causing lfs->seed % lfs->block_count to trigger SIGFPE and denial of service.
Use of uninitialized memory when processing certain font files in X.Org libXfont before 2.0.10 could be used by authenticated attackers to crash the X server.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing ownership verification in Feedback activity templates allows an authenticated teacher to view, use, or delete templates associated with courses other than their own. This can result in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of course materials.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to missing ownership checks in badge alignments, an authenticated user with badge management privileges can view and modify alignments associated with badges they do not own. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data disclosure and tampering with badge configurations.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing authorization checks in the forum discussion web services allow authenticated users to view discussion information in courses they do not have permission to access. In addition, users with teacher privileges may lock forum discussions in courses where they lack proper authorization. This issue can lead to unauthorized information disclosure and unauthorized discussion state modification.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when editing Lesson activity pages, authenticated users with teacher privileges can view and move lesson pages from courses they are not permitted to access into their own lessons. This issue can lead to unauthorized access and modification of restricted course content.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz editing functionality allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to view slot details and modify sections of quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this flaw to alter quiz configurations or disclose quiz structure information without proper authorization.
In JetBrains Ktor before 3.6.1 a DoS attack was possible via the CIO engine

A flaw was found in GIMP. Opening a crafted XCF with a truncated uncompressed tile can expose uninitialized main-process stack memory through the imported layer's pixel data, which may include process addresses that weaken ASLR.

Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform. Prior to 3.4.2, an unauthenticated user can submit a PNG to POST /upload, which reaches aperisolve/utils/png.py through analyze_image, PCRTAnalyzer, PNG.repair(), and check_idat(). A malformed IDAT chunk can make attacker-controlled length and newline data drive an unbounded combinations search in PNG._fix_dos2unix(), causing repeated CRC checks that occupy a worker and delay or block image analysis for other users. Per-IP upload limits and eventual job termination bound the denial of service, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.2.

Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the authenticated URL-upload endpoint and authenticated embed endpoint fetch user-supplied URLs server-side without protection against internal targets, allowing an attacker with the applicable backend permission to cause the Bolt server to request those targets. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

@fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

The publicly distributed InfoScan Electron installer contains configuration files identifying hostnames associated with customer installations and internal development, testing, and database infrastructure. An individual who obtains and inspects the installer can extract these hostnames without authenticating to the affected systems.

InfoScan does not enforce authentication on an endpoint used to retrieve sales-automation templates. A local attacker can submit an HTTP request to the affected endpoint without a valid session and retrieve the returned template data.

InfoScan contains an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability in its mobile-enumeration and version-reporting endpoints. A remote attacker can send HTTP requests without authentication to retrieve system configuration information, including usernames and display names, multifactor authentication configuration status, session settings, application version information, server details, hardware module firmware versions, and the BACnet/IP port used by the installation.

InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that return detailed Node.js stack traces to the requester. The responses disclose internal filesystem paths, application directory names, source file locations, and line numbers.

@fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions up to and including 10.1.11, when it is configured to deny or ignore dotfiles together with directory listing enabled, a request for a denied dot-directory returns its directory listing instead of being refused. The underlying send step answers with a forbidden response, but the listing fallback misreads that response on a path ending in a slash as a directory without an index file and serves the listing anyway. An unauthenticated client can enumerate the names of files and subdirectories, recursively, inside dot-directories the operator explicitly denied, such as version control, backup, and key file names. File contents remain protected and only names are disclosed. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.12, and users should upgrade to 10.1.12 or later. As a workaround, disable directory listing or do not serve a root that contains dot-directories.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

The MongoDB Ruby driver can include unmasked connection string content in the error it raises when a connection string cannot be parsed. If that connection string carries a secret, the secret may be disclosed in cleartext through the application's error output or logs. No privileges on the driver and no network access are needed to produce the error; a party able to read the application's error output may obtain the secret.

A credential-handling weakness in the MongoDB Python Driver allows a configuration option value that protects private key material to be written in clear text into the embedding application's own output and log records when a driver object is converted to text. A party able to read that output may obtain the credential. Obtaining it requires read access to the application's local output or log files.

The MongoDB PHP extension includes the full connection string it was given in the error it raises when that string cannot be parsed. A party able to influence any part of the connection string, including a part that holds no secret, can cause the resulting message to carry credentials into the application's standard error output and log files. This may result in unintended disclosure of authentication material to anyone able to read that output.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could make unauthorized changes when restoring archived indexed data or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) on the Splunk Enterprise instance.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not require the indexes_edit capability for archived-data restoration actions.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
For more information see Restore archived indexed data (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-indexers-and-indexer-clusters/10.6/back-up-and-archive-your-indexes/restore-archived-indexed-data) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands into a Classic Dashboard search. When another user opens the affected dashboard in Splunk Web, those injected commands execute with the viewing user's permissions, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to access stored credentials and write data to indexes.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape user-supplied content when it rewrites a search, which lets the rewritten search include additional SPL commands.
The vulnerability requires another user to open the dashboard in Splunk Web. Consequently, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) and Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could inject arbitrary fields into Splunk Enterprise audit records via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. 
Successful exploitation could allow the unauthenticated user to forge audit evidence, compromising the integrity of audit reviews and security detections that rely on legacy audit-field parsing.
The vulnerability exists because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize field delimiters in user-supplied data before writing the data to a legacy audit record. The affected workflow also does not create a corresponding structured audit record.
For more information see Auditing activities in a Splunk platform instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.0/audit-activity-in-splunk-enterprise/auditing-activities-in-a-splunk-platform-instance) and About structured audit trail logs (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/audit-activity-in-splunk-enterprise/about-structured-audit-trail-logs) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled asset data in an asset source lookup. A user that holds a role with the mc_assets_read capability could later open the Asset Center dashboard and select that value in the Asset Information table. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of that user. With this access, the user who stored the asset data could expose or modify data available to the user who selected the value.
The vulnerability is possible because Asset Center does not escape asset values before adding them to drilldown searches.
The vulnerability requires Asset Center to process the asset data and another user to select the value. The user who stored the data should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security), Add asset and identity data to Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/asset-and-identity-management/add-asset-and-identity-data-to-splunk-enterprise-security), and Asset and identity dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/asset-and-identity-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an authenticated user who does not hold the edit_correlationsearches capability could set Status to Testing for a versioned detection or clear that setting. This could affect the integrity and availability of detection testing.
The vulnerability is possible because the Test Mode Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not require the edit_correlationsearches capability before it creates or deletes scheduled test copies of detections.
