For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Test detections on production data using Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/detections/test-detections-on-production-data-using-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in the Malware data model. Another authenticated user with access to the Malware Search dashboard could later select a table row containing those values. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the row. The commands could expose data available to the user who selected the row and add attacker-controlled records to an index.
The vulnerability is possible because the Malware Search dashboard does not safely quote row values before adding them to drilldown searches.
For more information see Endpoint dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.4/analytics/endpoint-dashboards) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could run a search that causes attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) text to appear in the Search Audit dashboard. If another user who can access the dashboard selects the affected search, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled SPL commands using the permissions of the user who selects the search. The user who runs the first search could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the affected search.
The vulnerability is possible because the Search Audit dashboard does not safely escape logged search text before inserting it into drilldown searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Audit dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/audit-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in vulnerability data. If another user who can access the Vulnerability Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Vulnerability Search dashboard encodes data-model field values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Network dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/network-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in managed-lookup audit data. If another user who can access the Managed Lookups Audit dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Managed Lookups Audit dashboard does not safely escape audit data before inserting it into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Audit dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/audit-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in endpoint summary data. If another user who can access the Time Center dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Time Center dashboard does not safely escape endpoint summary values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Endpoint dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/endpoint-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data used by the Weak Encrypted Communication report. If another user who can access the report selects an affected drilldown, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the drilldown. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the drilldown.
The vulnerability is possible because the Weak Encrypted Communication report does not validate source, destination, and Secure Sockets Layer version values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Weak Encrypted Communication (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/weak-encrypted-communication) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to edit containers for an allowed label could forge the author attribution of container pins and access limited user details outside the expected authorization boundary.
The Container Pin Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not prevent caller-provided author fields from reaching generic model binding, which lets the request reassign a pin author or query user-related data outside the expected authorization scope.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.3.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to create containers on one label could use the Representational State Transfer (REST) API to create a container with a parent relationship to a container that the user cannot access. This could let the user alter incident lineage across authorization boundaries and identify existing restricted containers.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API accepts a customer-supplied parent relationship when creating a container without authorizing access to the referenced container.
For more information see REST Containers (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.6.0/container-endpoints/rest-containers) and Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to view and edit containers and at least one container label could set misleading user and app provenance on containers that the user creates and learn whether user IDs and installed app identifiers exist.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API accepts client-supplied values for server-managed container fields.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to create and view containers for a label could use the Representational State Transfer (REST) API to create a container that references a workbook phase in a case the user cannot view, disclosing the phase name and creating an inconsistent phase association.
The vulnerability exists because the Container REST API does not enforce the same case-scoped authorization when it accepts a workbook-phase reference during container creation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with container edit permission could supply timestamps when creating containers and artifacts through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could alter the timeline shown to analysts and cause configured data retention strategies to delete affected records earlier than intended.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API accepts client-supplied values for timestamps that Splunk SOAR uses to order records and apply data retention.
The early deletion impact requires an applicable data retention strategy; the timeline impact does not.
For more information see Manage your PostgreSQL database with data retention strategies (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/manage-your-postgresql-database-with-data-retention-strategies) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to author and run playbooks could add messages to a different playbook run log and cause that run to fail, including runs outside the labels that the user could access.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify that playbook API requests use the trusted runtime context for the current playbook run.

In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, an unauthenticated user could cause Splunk App for Stream to reset its in-memory indexer cache.
The vulnerability exists because the Splunk Web handler accepts the cache-reset request without requiring a login.
For more information see Splunk Stream installation package overview (https://help.splunk.com/en/data-management/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.0/introduction/splunk-stream-installation-package-overview) and Launch Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.6/administer-splunk-enterprise-with-splunk-web/launch-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared data model.
The vulnerability is possible because the Data Model Editor does not properly neutralize data model field names when it builds a preview search.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Add a regular expression field (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/define-data-model-dataset-fields/add-a-regular-expression-field), Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities), and About the search language (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.4/search-overview/about-the-search-language) in the Splunk documentation.

Insufficient verification of data authenticity in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in AWS SDK for PHP before 3.383.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to forge ciphertext that decrypts to arbitrary plaintext via manipulation of the GCM authentication tag length metadata.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS SDK for PHP version 3.383.1 or later.

Certain EZVIZ devices are affected by an improper certificate validation issue (CWE-295). An attacker may intercept communication traffic to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack.

A vulnerability was identified in OpenZipkin Zipkin 3.6.1. This affects the function UnzippingBytesRequestConverter.convertRequest of the file zipkin-server/src/main/java/zipkin2/server/internal/ZipkinHttpCollector.java of the component HTTP Collector. Such manipulation leads to highly compressed data. The attack can be executed remotely. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

free5GC PCF through 1.4.6 contains a resource leak in postAppSessCtxProcedure that leaves PCC rules and QoS data in the SM policy decision after rejected Npcf_PolicyAuthorization create requests. Authenticated AFs knowing an active PDU session's UE address can send repeated failing requests with distinct AF application identifiers to grow PCF memory and pollute policy sent to the SMF.

This issue affects Tegsoft İletişim Merkezi: before latest-202611161510.

Inscriptis is a Python library for converting HTML to text. From 2.0.0 until 2.7.6, when the parent is block-level, table_end_handler() in model/tag/table_tag.py writes each sibling table through HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text() in model/html_element.py; Canvas.open_block() leaves the parent padding_inline prefix on the stack, Canvas.close_block() does not remove it, and only Canvas.close_tag() calls prefix.remove_last_prefix(). Each following sibling table therefore carries forward accumulated indentation, making get_text() output grow quadratically and allowing small attacker-controlled HTML to exhaust memory in applications converting it without authentication or user interaction. This issue is fixed in 2.7.6.

A flaw was found in the quarkus-rest-jsonb component of Quarkus. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP requests containing deeply nested JSON payloads to vulnerable endpoints. The application fails during JSON parsing and records an excessively large error trace for each small request. This disproportionate log amplification can exhaust system disk space or overwhelm log processing pipelines, degrading service availability.

Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc4 and earlier, org.freedesktop.Avahi.Server.RecordBrowserNew accepts a domain-name value that avahi_is_valid_domain_name considers valid even though avahi_normalize_name_strdup cannot normalize it. The resulting null key reaches the key assertion in dbus_prepare_record_browser_object. A local low-privileged D-Bus client can trigger the mismatch and terminate the Avahi daemon, causing denial of service. The issue is fixed in 0.9-rc5.

Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the file access checks in Amazon awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server 1.0.10 through 1.0.20 might allow a context-dependent actor, via crafted document content processed by an MCP client, to read files outside the intended base directory and, in 1.0.12 through 1.0.20, to write PNG slide images outside it. This occurs when DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR is not set or is empty and the CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST environment variable is present. Versions before 1.0.10 do not restrict file access to a base directory.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.0.21 or later. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can set DOCUMENT_BASE_DIR to the directory that holds their documents. Do not set it to /, which removes the restriction.

codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.1-rc.1, the optional graph UI's POST /api/process-kill route omitted the indexing-job ownership check on Windows while retaining that check on POSIX systems. A requester able to reach the optional UI could supply an arbitrary process identifier, causing TerminateProcess to stop any process that the server user was permitted to terminate. The flaw affects the Windows-specific process termination path and can cause a high availability impact without disclosing or modifying data. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.1-rc.1.

codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.10.0, the indexer's .gitignore matcher implemented * and ** through recursive backtracking without a work bound. A repository containing a pattern with repeated wildcard groups and a long path could make matching work grow exponentially, allowing a single ignore rule to stall discovery indefinitely and, before worker isolation, stall the server. The impact is limited to availability, and the bounded matcher does not claim that every expensive input is eliminated. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.

U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to access a vulnerable endpoint that returns a list of application users and their permissions in plaintext. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

A flaw has been found in highlight highlight.js up to 11.12.0. The affected element is the function hljs.highlight of the file src/languages/livescript.js of the component Language Grammar Handler. Executing a manipulation of the argument text can lead to inefficient regular expression complexity. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

probe-image-size 7.4.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in lib/common/svg_header.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to block the event loop via crafted SVG doctypes. Attackers can supply SVGs with an unclosed internal subset followed by many ']' characters to trigger quadratic backtracking in probe.sync, probe(stream) or probe(url), causing repeated event loop stalls.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in lib/parse_stream/avif.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via attacker-declared ftyp or meta box sizes. Attackers can supply an AVIF stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge box length, forcing the parser to buffer all received bytes and causing denial of service.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory buffering vulnerability in parseExif in lib/parse_stream/webp.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via an attacker-declared EXIF chunk length. Attackers can supply a WebP stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge EXIF length after VP8X, causing unbounded buffering and process memory exhaustion.

Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in rx_ip6() checksum validation that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read past received packets by sending IPv6 extension headers. Attackers can send a single IPv6 TCP or ICMPv6 packet with extension headers, causing tcp6csum_ok() and icmp6csum_ok() to use the full payload length and read adjacent receive-buffer memory.
This issue was addressed with improved checks. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, visionOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2. An app may be able to access sensitive user data.

An out-of-bounds read was addressed with improved bounds checking. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2. Processing a maliciously crafted font may result in the disclosure of process memory.

The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not exclude donors who chose to give anonymously from one of its public REST API listings, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve those donors' names.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check authorization, or whether a meeting is restricted to logged-in users, password-protected or unpublished, before returning a meeting's join links, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the passcode-embedded join links of any meeting, including meetings the site restricts.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that a requested Zoom meeting's recordings were published on the site before fetching them with the site's connected Zoom account, allowing unauthenticated users who know a meeting ID to retrieve that meeting's cloud recording details, including its topic, share link, passcode when returned by Zoom, and direct play and download links.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not check that a visitor is really the subscriber before showing them newsletters marked as private, and accepts a weaker subscriber identifier that anyone can obtain by submitting a known subscriber's email address to the public subscription form, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a subscriber's email address to read every private newsletter sent to that subscriber.

The Payment forms, Buy now buttons, and Invoicing System | GetPaid WordPress plugin before 2.8.63 does not check that the visitor is allowed to view an invoice before rendering it through its single-invoice shortcode, and its payment-form embed page lets unauthenticated users render that shortcode for any invoice ID, disclosing customers' names, billing addresses, phone numbers, line items and payment status.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not apply the per-link visibility rules of space sidebar links when listing spaces in its space discovery feature, allowing unauthenticated visitors to retrieve the titles and URLs of links restricted to logged-in users or specific memberships, as well as disabled links, for every public and private space.

The Social Media Auto Poster – Schedule & Publish to Buffer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.9. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to delete Buffer sync log history for and disclose Buffer sync log contents of arbitrary posts, including those authored by administrators. The nonce used as the sole gate is not bound to any specific post ID, so a nonce harvested from the attacker's own draft editor screen is valid against any arbitrary post ID submitted in the request.

The MailerLite – Signup forms (official) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.27 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to approve a comment containing the malicious shortcode, after which any page rendering the Latest Comments block with excerpts enabled will trigger the injected script for all visitors.

The ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the administrator to have enabled the 'Deliver WebP/AVIF images using the ShortPixel CDN' (useCDN) option, after which any unauthenticated visitor can submit a comment containing a crafted url() payload inside an allowed HTML construct such as <acronym title="...">, which WordPress comment kses preserves on save; the dangerous attribute-boundary breakout occurs only at render time inside the ob_start output-buffer rewriter, where kses does not apply.

The Redux Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<opt_name>[<color-field-id>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post() sanitization applied via Redux_Helpers::sanitize_array() is bypassed — not broken — because an <a class="thickbox" title="&lt;img onerror=...&gt;"> payload uses only kses-allowed tags and attributes, with the entity-encoded onerror handler surviving storage as inert text that the browser decodes when WordPress core's thickbox.js reads the title attribute and writes it into the modal as HTML. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HyperlinkObject.label (percent-encoded)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.92 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the WordPress site to have a published Anonymous-access Registration Form app configured against a table with a HyperlinkObject column, and a legacy Data Project list using a $$link$$ Dynamic Hyperlink against that same column; given this configuration, any unauthenticated visitor can plant the payload.

The Speed Booster Pack ⚡ PageSpeed Optimization Suite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the plugin's Lazy load media option is enabled and that the attacker's comment is approved by a site administrator or via auto-approval.

The Real Cookie Banner: GDPR & ePrivacy Cookie Consent plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.4.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the cookie banner has been activated by the site administrator (the plugin's primary onboarding step) and that at least one prior comment from the same name and email identity has already been approved, after which WordPress core's comment_previously_approved default auto-approves subsequent comments without administrator action.

The ProfilePress – Paid Membership, Online Courses (LMS), Ecommerce, User Registration & Login Form, User Profile & Restrict Content plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.0 via the 'sortby<form_id>, filter<form_id>' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract reconstruct any listed member's full e-mail address one character at a time via a boolean LIKE oracle, and enumerate users holding arbitrary usermeta keys such as ppress_billing_phone. The e-mail address oracle is reachable on any default install that used the plugin's 'Create pages' onboarding notice, because pp_email_address is enabled as a search field by default and the resulting directory page is published with no capability or nonce gate.

The GPTranslate – Multilingual AI Translation Agent for WordPress: Translate Your Site with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.34.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the plugin's non-default 'HTML DOM method' to be enabled for server-side translation, and a translation row for the target language-prefixed URL must exist to arm the output buffer that routes page content through the vulnerable Simple HTML DOM parser.

An object dictionary entry can carry write-access flags and still have a NULL data pointer, for example when a constant value is held in the value field rather than in addressable storage. The CoE SDO download handler checked write access but not whether storage was present, then wrote the master-supplied payload through the NULL pointer.

The CoE SDO upload handler enters its normal-response path (used for objects longer than 4 bytes) and passes (objd + nsub)->data directly to the pre-object handler and to the response copy. Entries that hold a constant in the value field have data set to NULL; a master can request such an entry and cause a NULL pointer dereference in the upload path.

ESC_foeprocess can be reached by an incoming mailbox frame before the application calls FOE_config to supply the file table and flush buffer pointers. When foe_cfg or its fbuffer field is NULL the handler dereferenced those pointers while processing the frame, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

ESC_eoeprocess and ESC_eoeprocess_tx can be reached before the application calls EOE_config to supply the callback table pointer. When eoe_cfg is NULL the receive handler dereferenced it while processing an incoming EoE frame, and the transmit polling function dereferenced it on each cycle, causing NULL pointer dereferences.

An object dictionary entry that holds a constant has no process data storage and carries a NULL data pointer. sizeOfPDO did not check for this when resolving a mapped entry to its descriptor. A master that maps such an entry to a PDO causes COE_pdoPack or COE_pdoUnpack to dereference the NULL data pointer on every process data exchange after the mapping is activated.

The CoE complete-access download handler iterated over all subindices of an object and wrote the master-supplied payload into each writable entry. Entries that hold a constant have write-access flags set but carry a NULL data pointer. The handler did not check for this and wrote the master payload through the NULL pointer.

@fastify/rate-limit is the rate-limiting plugin for the Fastify web framework. Starting in version 11.1.0, the plugin documented a manual flow for limiting failed login attempts that peeks at the limiter, runs the password check, and consumes a slot only on failure. Because the peek and the consume are two separate store operations with the password check in between, concurrent requests can all pass the peek before any slot is consumed, so in versions 11.1.0 through 11.2.2 a burst of requests runs far more failed attempts than the configured limit, and the sequential path also allowed one attempt more than configured. The default per-request limiter is not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/rate-limit 11.3.0, which makes the manual flow atomic by reserving a slot in a single operation and refunding it only on success, and users should upgrade to 11.3.0 or later.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject JavaScript by saving a crafted value in their STREET profile field. Attackers can break out of the unencoded title attribute in members_assignment_data.php with an onmouseover handler that executes in the session of role managers hovering over the address icon.

Admidio from 5.0.16 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with folder upload rights to store JavaScript by uploading SVG files served inline. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG that downloadFile() serves as image/svg+xml inline without nosniff or CSP, executing on the Admidio origin for viewers including unauthenticated visitors.

Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in modules/profile/profile_new.php that allows authenticated Group Leaders to bypass field-level profile restrictions. Attackers can request mode=html_selection to read restricted field values and submit mode=save requests to modify restricted member profile fields.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains a guard bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute write subqueries by embedding them in LIVE query WHERE clauses or field projections. Attackers can inject CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, or RELATE statements that run atomically inside other users' triggering transactions, amplifying writes and exfiltrating document data after permission revocation.

Rclone from 1.56.0 before 1.76.0 contains a timing side-channel vulnerability in its htpasswd authentication middleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate valid usernames. Attackers can send HTTP Basic Auth requests with wrong passwords and measure response times, because bcrypt verification runs only for existing users, enabling targeted password guessing.

AzuraCast before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the /api/station/{station_id}/profile/edit endpoint that exposes and accepts Icecast/Shoutcast passwords for users holding Manage Station Profile without Manage Station Broadcasting. Authenticated station users can read the admin, source, relay and streamer passwords via GET to administer Icecast or broadcast to listeners, or overwrite them via PUT to lock out operators.

AzuraCast 0.19.0 before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows users with station media rights to add tracks to other stations' playlists by supplying foreign playlist ids to the single-file edit endpoint. Attackers can send sequential playlist ids in the playlists array to inject entries into other stations' AutoDJ rotations and public now-playing metadata, causing failed playback slots.

Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.121.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Utilities module endpoint that lets any authenticated user retry failed bulk transactions without a role check. Attackers, including portal users with no roles, can send crafted requests for a chosen date to mark site-wide failed bulk transactions as retried, removing them from the normal recovery path, and add background job load.

Frappe ERPNext 12.7.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 stores imported Italian supplier e-invoices as public files in the Regional module, which the server returns without authentication. Unauthenticated attackers can request predictable file URLs built from the supplier's VAT number and invoice sequence to read supplier names, VAT numbers, bank account details and line items.

Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CRM module because notes on Leads and Opportunities are saved without passing through the HTML sanitiser. Authenticated users with the Sales User role can save a note containing a crafted payload that executes in another user's session when they open the record, acting with that user's permissions.

A weakness has been identified in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.7.2. This vulnerability affects the function guardToolExecution of the file packages/agent-core-v2/src/features/plan/planService.ts of the component Plan Mode Permission Guard. Executing a manipulation can lead to improper authorization. The attack requires local access. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security vulnerability has been detected in ggml-org llama.cpp 0.7.0-dev. This affects the function common_sampler_init of the file common/sampling.cpp of the component llama-server. Such manipulation of the argument grammar_triggers[].type leads to improper input validation. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version b12405 mitigates this issue. The name of the patch is 9f26fe11c73c7e74a5e99e7f1b6370ad8e1cb22d. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that casts target nodes to GF_ParentNode without validation. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT-A file whose command targets a non-grouping node, causing gf_node_list_get_child() to perform an invalid memory read and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_odf_encode_ui_config() in src/odf/descriptors.c that allows attackers to crash the process. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file declaring an interaction stream without a UIConfig descriptor, causing a denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in src/compositor/mpeg4_sensors.c that allows attackers to crash the process via uninitialized sensor nodes. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that makes compositor_mpeg4_get_sensor_handler_ex() call hs->IsEnabled through a near-NULL pointer, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader because xmt_node_end() frees unattached nodes but leaves them on the parser node stack. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file whose text content makes xmt_text_content() pass the freed node to gf_node_get_tag(), reading freed heap memory and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in xmt_discard_subtree() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to exhaust the call stack. Attackers can persuade a user to process a crafted XMT file with deeply nested discarded SFNode and MFNode fields to crash MP4Box.

Freedit before 0.9.9 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the post_lock, post_hide, post_pin and comment_hide handlers that allows inn moderators to act on content from other inns. Attackers can supply their own inn id with a foreign post or comment id to lock or hide content instance-wide, or pin private posts to expose titles.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in TraverseForm() in src/compositor/mpeg4_form.c due to an off-by-one groupsIndex bounds check. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with a Form node having constraints but an empty groupsIndex field to crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_instantiate() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c that lacks cycle detection or depth limits. Attackers can craft an XMT scene whose PROTO body instantiates itself directly or indirectly, exhausting the stack and crashing MP4Box when imported.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in xmt_remove_od_links_recursive() in loader_xmt.c that lacks any depth limit when walking node children. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with deeply nested or cyclic node and SFCommandBuffer references to exhaust the stack and crash MP4Box on import.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that misinterprets single node values as child lists for MFNode field replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that causes an invalid node pointer to be dereferenced by gf_node_register(), crashing MP4Box for denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c when handling MFNode field replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with an MFNode field replace command lacking a node value to crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in JSScript_LoadVRML() in src/scenegraph/vrml_js.c that reads unchecked script_text pointers of Script node url entries. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene loading a Script node whose url entry lacks script text, crashing MP4Box and causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the application by supplying a crafted XMT scene. Attackers can modify InputSensor, Layout or EnvironmentTest nodes during parsing, triggering compositor handlers that read uninitialized private stacks and cause denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_create_node() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c when cloning PROTO instances. Attackers can craft an XMT scene declaring more PROTO interface fields than the cloned instance supplies, crashing MP4Box when a user opens the file.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() that allows attackers to crash the application via indexed field-replace commands lacking a payload. Attackers can craft an XMT scene whose GF_SG_XREPLACE command on an MFNode field carries no value, causing a crash and denial of service when opened.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in ctxload_process() in src/filters/load_bt_xmt.c that casts object descriptor update entries without checking the descriptor tag. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BT scene placing a different descriptor type in a GF_ODUpdate command, causing gf_list_get() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in curve2d_check_changes() that casts a Curve2D point field node to M_Coordinate2D without type checking. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BIFS scene placing another node type such as LinearGradient in that field, causing an invalid pointer read that crashes the process.

Members WordPress plugin by MemberPress 3.2.28 before 3.3.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to evade Private Site mode via login page exemption. Attackers can request the front-end login path with a pagename query variable to make WordPress render hidden published pages or the full blog index.

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read comments on role-restricted posts via the Latest Comments block. Attackers can view pages hosting the block, where get_the_ID() checks the host page and get_comment_excerpt() bypasses filtering, exposing restricted comments, post titles, and links.

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read role-restricted posts by viewing Latest Posts blocks in full-content mode. The block renders raw post_content without firing the_content filter, bypassing members_content_permissions_protect() and exposing complete bodies of restricted posts.

WPGSI: Spreadsheet Integration before 3.8.5 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to delete posts by abusing the delete action in wpgsi_show_view() without nonce verification. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into following a crafted wpgsi-show link with action=delete and an id parameter to delete arbitrary posts or pages.

graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the parser max_tokens limit using long runs of comments. Attackers can submit GraphQL documents of consecutive comments that Lexer.lookahead fully tokenizes before limit checks, consuming CPU and memory proportional to document size.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 contains a link following vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to read host files by setting --eventpath in an untrusted project .actrc to a symlink. Attackers can commit an event.json symlink pointing to files like ~/.ssh/id_rsa, which act copies into the job container as GITHUB_EVENT_PATH for workflow steps to exfiltrate.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.19.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the sanitize-svg function that allows authenticated users to bypass filtering through unescaped re-serialization. Attackers with file edit permission can upload SVGs using entity-encoded or CDATA-wrapped markup or attribute quote breakouts to execute JavaScript in the Penpot origin when victims open them.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read unpublished help center articles through the public portal API. Attackers can request archived articles by slug via the ArticlesController show actions or read draft translations exposed through associated_articles in article JSON responses.

RSSHub before 2026.11.01-8521.e529e9b contains a domain validation bypass in the javdb routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to capture the operator's JAVDB_SESSION cookie. Attackers can pass an absolute javdb.com URL in the category parameter and set the domain query to a host they control, causing processItems to send the _jdb_session cookie there.

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in Nextcloud.get_file that allows authenticated recipe editors to write and delete files by using unsanitized recipe names in temporary paths. Attackers can set a recipe name containing ../ segments via PATCH /api/recipe/<pk>/ and request /api/get_recipe_file/<pk>/ to overwrite and remove .pdf files outside the temporary directory.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an invalid pointer dereference vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportEmbeddedTextures that derives the texture format hint without checking the strchr result. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with an embedded image mime type lacking a slash to crash the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use of uninitialized resource vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that builds TRIANGLE_STRIP and TRIANGLE_FAN faces from unfilled faces. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file whose strip or fan primitives trigger out-of-bounds reads or null pointer dereferences, crashing the importing application.

Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SkipLine that allows attackers to hang parsing by supplying files with '#' comment lines. Attackers can provide crafted OFF, LWS, or MD3 shader files so ReadFile never returns, consuming a CPU core and denying service.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in FBXConverter::GetRotationKeyframeList that allows attackers to exhaust memory via unbounded rotation angle differences. Attackers can supply a crafted FBX file of about 111 KB whose keyframe interpolation loop never advances, consuming gigabytes of memory until the importing process is killed.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ColladaParser::ReadPrimitives that allows attackers to exhaust memory via non-numeric index values. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose

index list contains a non-digit character, causing endless zero-index appends until the importing process crashes.

A flaw has been found in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.5. This affects the function ASEImporter::InternReadFile of the file code/AssetLib/ASE/ASELoader.cpp of the component ASE File Importer. This manipulation causes out-of-bounds write. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 6.0.6 mitigates this issue. Patch name: 7ccc44a338dcdcc81023484388126ab1a8250e94. You should upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability was found in Webkul Bagisto up to 2.4.13. Affected is the function RazorpayController::paymentSuccess of the file packages/Webkul/Razorpay/src/Http/Controllers/RazorpayController.php of the component Payment Gateway Success/Callback Controllers. Performing a manipulation results in insufficient verification of data authenticity. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. Upgrading to version 2.4.14 is able to address this issue. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

A weakness has been identified in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.6. The affected element is the function Assimp::ColladaLoader::CreateAnimation of the file code/AssetLib/Collada/ColladaLoader.cpp of the component Collada Loader. This manipulation of the argument mSize causes out-of-bounds write. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.6. The impacted element is the function Assimp::JoinVerticesProcess::ProcessMesh of the file code/PostProcessing/JoinVerticesProcess.cpp of the component PostProcessing JoinVerticesProcess. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was detected in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.5. This affects the function Assimp::PretransformVertices::BuildMeshRefCountArray of the file PretransformVertices.cpp. Performing a manipulation results in out-of-bounds write. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in Bagisto MangoPay Payment Gateway up to c061edcc7973cb37a77a9f9ae523db170c3e28ed. Affected by this vulnerability is the function MangoPayStandardController::success of the file src/Http/Controllers/Shop/MangoPayStandardController.php of the component Success Callback. The manipulation leads to insufficient verification of data authenticity. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. This product follows a rolling release approach for continuous delivery, so version details for affected or updated releases are not provided.

A vulnerability was identified in code-projects Intern Record System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file /department.sql. Such manipulation leads to file and directory information exposure. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

A security flaw has been discovered in warpdesign pcx-js up to 1.1.1. Affected is the function decode8bpp/decode4bpp of the file js/pcx.js of the component PCX Pixel Buffer Decoder. Performing a manipulation results in uncontrolled memory allocation. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in shaozilee bmp-js up to 0.1.0. This vulnerability affects the function BmpDecoder.parseRGBA of the file lib/decoder.js. This manipulation causes uncontrolled memory allocation. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability has been found in vthibault tga-js up to 1.1.1. This issue affects the function _decodeRLE of the file src/tga.js of the component TgaLoader. Such manipulation leads to uncontrolled memory allocation. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability was determined in kchapelier qoijs 1.0.0. The affected element is the function decode of the file src/decode.js of the component QOI Decoder. Executing a manipulation of the argument arrayBuffer can lead to uncontrolled memory allocation. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability was identified in Snes9x up to 1.63. The impacted element is the function S9xUnfreezeFromStream of the file snapshot.cpp of the component Save-State Screenshot Restoration. The manipulation leads to out-of-bounds read. The attack must be carried out locally. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability has been found in osCommerce up to 4.14.63493. This affects the function actionCached of the file lib/frontend/controllers/ImageController.php of the component Cached Image Handler. The manipulation of the argument image leads to path traversal. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Improper access control in the repository access request endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged user to self-approve an access request via an out-of-range vault type value that skips the approval check.

PodFetch 5.2.0 before 5.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Audiobookshelf-compatible POST /api/podcasts endpoint that allows authenticated low-privilege users to add podcasts by bypassing role and USER_PODCAST_LIMIT checks. Attackers with the plain user role can submit attacker-chosen feed URLs in media.metadata.feedUrl to force server-side fetching and episode downloads, consuming disk and bandwidth.

The weDevs Subscribe2 WordPress plugin 10.35 before 10.50 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remove public subscribers by forging the s2_unsub GET parameter. Attackers can base64-encode a known subscriber email and visit any page with the subscribe2 shortcode to delete that subscriber from the mailing list.

Sim 0.5.61 before 0.9.41 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows write-level workspace members to change workflow MCP server visibility without admin permission. Attackers can set isPublic via POST or PATCH to /api/mcp/workflow-servers, exposing deployed workflows to unauthenticated invocation through /api/mcp/serve.

CISO Assistant before 4.2.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to block all logins by exhausting a shared rate limit keyed on the frontend server IP. Attackers can send a low sustained rate of failed login attempts through the SvelteKit frontend to exhaust the django-allauth per-address budget, locking out every user.

LibRaw 0.22.0 through 0.22.3 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in HuffTable::len() because parse_dht() stores Huffman DC symbols without validating them as difference categories. Attackers can supply a crafted TIFF/ARW file with oversized Huffman symbols in a Sony YCbCr lossless JPEG stream to crash applications decoding it, causing denial of service.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability. An unauthenticated adjacent network attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a denial of service condition.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use TLS 1.3 early data using the ssl_early_data on directive, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS 1.3 connection to drive an NGINX worker into a tight loop in which it repeatedly retries the same send without ever making progress. The worker continues accepting new connections and handling existing ones, but one CPU core is pinned at 100%.

Impact:
System performance can degrade until the NGINX worker process is either forced to restart or is manually restarted. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a degradation of service that can lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Plane before 1.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in WorkspaceDraftIssueViewSet that allows authenticated workspace members to create drafts in unauthorized projects by supplying an arbitrary project_id. Attackers can convert drafts into work items in private or removed-from projects with chosen title, state, assignees, cycle_id and module_ids, triggering notifications and disclosing project membership.

AiSOC before 23.6.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the agents service that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' investigation runs by supplying their run_id. Attackers can query GET /api/v1/investigations/{run_id}, report variants, the WebSocket stream, or agent-runs routes to obtain audit logs, forensic output, and incident reports.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability. An unauthenticated remote attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a denial of service condition.

phpwcms before 1.9.53, 1.12.7 and 2.0.0-beta.4 contains a host header poisoning vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to control password reminder links by sending a forged X-Forwarded-Host header. Attackers can submit the public password reminder form for a victim so the emailed {LOGIN_URL} points to an attacker host, capturing the new password when the victim logs in there.

LiteLLM Proxy 1.62.4 before 1.84.0 contains a callback injection vulnerability that allows authenticated API key holders to register process-wide logging callbacks by supplying callbacks fields in request bodies. Attackers can name an unenabled observability integration such as langsmith or langfuse to leak all users' prompts and responses, or suppress operator logging via litellm_disabled_callbacks.

ERPSaaS 3.7.9 through 3.47.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated company users to inject script markup through unescaped client and company address fields. Attackers can store script in address lines rendered by getFormattedAddressHtml() via unescaped Blade output, executing in browsers of users viewing, previewing or printing invoices and estimates.

OpenCV through 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 through 5.1.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in YAMLParser::parse that allows attackers to cause denial of service via crafted YAML dash lines. Attackers can supply YAML files with a non-separator '-' line after the first document, opened through cv::FileStorage, to hang the thread at full CPU.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in rpl_remove_routes_by_nexthop() in the RPL-Classic implementation that allows adjacent attackers to crash nodes. Attackers participating in the RPL network can create a stale route whose next-hop neighbor entry was removed, then trigger parent removal to crash the node.

LibreCAD through 2.2.1.6 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in RS_FilterDXF1::readFileInBuffer() caused by unvalidated truncation of the 64-bit file size. Attackers can persuade users to open a crafted DXF file sized 0xFFFFFFF8 bytes, writing a NUL byte before an 8-byte buffer to corrupt heap metadata and crash the application.

MyBibliotheca 3.0.0 before 3.0.4 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify or delete other users' books via /api/v1/books/<book_id>. Attackers can obtain book UUIDs from recently added books across all owners, then send PUT or DELETE requests to rename, alter, or permanently delete them.

Anchr before 3.7.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to host HTML files by uploading them through the image upload feature with a spoofed image content type. Attackers can upload an .html file served via GET /api/image/:id from the Anchr origin, running script that steals the victim's localStorage session token for account takeover.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an uninitialized pointer dereference vulnerability because the File_Mpeg4_Descriptors constructor leaves the IsCmaf pointer holding stale heap contents. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with an AAC/USAC decoder specific descriptor so File_Usac::Streams_Finish_Conformance_Profile dereferences an invalid address, crashing the application.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in TimeCode::FromString() that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying hour-unit timestamps with fewer than three fractional digits. Attackers can craft a TTML file whose begin or end attribute contains such a timestamp, causing MediaInfo or embedding applications to crash with SIGFPE when opened.

Several Bluetooth LE Audio services in subsys/bluetooth/audio register global connection and authentication callbacks but assume every connection is LE. When CONFIG_BT_CLASSIC is enabled, the host also invokes these callbacks for BR/EDR connections. For such connections bt_conn_get_dst() returns NULL, and bt_conn_get_info() leaves info.le.dst unset (zero or uninitialized stack data). The CSIP Set Member (csip_disconnected(), handle_csip_disconnect(), handle_csip_auth_complete()), PACS (pacs_auth_pairing_complete(), pacs_security_changed()) and HAS (security_changed(), client_alloc(), client_free()) callbacks then compare or copy a Bluetooth address through that NULL or uninitialized pointer.

A remote device within Bluetooth range can trigger this against a dual-mode device that exposes LE Audio server roles and accepts BR/EDR connections. Opening and closing a BR/EDR ACL link, with no pairing, reaches the CSIP Set Member disconnect path. Completing SSP pairing (for example Just Works) or encryption reaches the PACS and HAS paths.

The impact is denial of service. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, the device halts on an assertion (bt_keys_find_addr(), context_alloc()). On platforms that trap NULL or wild reads, it crashes. Otherwise, internal PACS/CSIP/HAS client state is corrupted with bogus addresses. The defects are reads only, and the attacker does not control the address that is dereferenced. The fix adds bt_conn_is_type(conn, BT_CONN_TYPE_LE) checks at the top of the affected callbacks.

A security flaw has been discovered in RainyGao DocSys up to 2.02.91. Affected by this vulnerability is the function downloadDocRS of the file src/com/DocSystem/controller/DocController.java. Performing a manipulation of the argument path results in path traversal. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Dynamic Product Gallery for WooCommerce before 3.6.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access or above to inject arbitrary JavaScript via the product_id attribute of the [wc_product_dgallery] and [wc_product_dynamic_gallery] shortcodes. The parse_shortcode_product_dynamic_gallery() function passes product_id only through esc_attr(), and get_gallery_main() prints it unescaped into the a3-wc-dynamic-gallery-init-inline-script inline script as part of a JavaScript variable name, so a value such as 342;alert(document.domain)// breaks out of the declaration. The injected script executes in the browser of any user who views the post, including editors or administrators who preview or approve it.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 6db6147, contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the GET /exports/checkNew endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to read the names of other users' finished exports and suppress their notifications. ExportsController trusts a user ID supplied by the browser without checking it against the authenticated session, and ExportService marks every export it returns as notified, so the owner never receives the notice that their export is ready.

A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. A temporary block can be released to a shared memory pool before deferred response writers finish using it, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same memory. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed.

A vulnerability has been found in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected by this vulnerability is the function hedwigcgi_main of the file hedwig.cgi. The manipulation leads to missing authentication. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.
Tanium addressed an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in Enforce Recovery Key Portal.

CleverReach WP before 1.5.28 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Article_Search controller that allows unauthenticated attackers to read non-public posts by supplying post IDs. Attackers can enumerate the id parameter in search requests to retrieve raw content of draft, pending, private, and password-protected posts and pages.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_lut2.c because the second input's pixel format is unrestricted when the output depth option is set. Attackers can supply crafted media such as monoblack BMP or PBM images to index beyond lookup tables, crashing applications or leaking heap contents into output video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the lut1d filter in libavfilter/vf_lut3d.c that allows attackers to read heap memory by supplying planar high bit depth samples above the nominal depth. Attackers can craft 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit planar RGB video processed with a large 1D LUT to crash applications or disclose heap contents in output pixels.
Zoraxy provided by Zoraxy Project does not add HttpOnly attribute to session cookies that allows an attacker to retrieve session cookies via a script executed on the browser.

An unauthenticated attacker can send an unsigned SAML single logout request to force users to log out of Grafana Enterprise instances configured for SAML single logout (improper signature verification).
A logical flaw vulnerability exists in the ZTE Nubia RedMagic 9S Pro+. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may compromise confidentiality.

Prevent Direct Access – Protect WordPress Files plugin before 2.8.9.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain protected file names and paths by requesting the dynamically generated robots.txt file, which appends Disallow rules containing attachment page URLs and direct _pda/ directory file paths for all protected media. Attackers can send an unauthenticated HTTP request to robots.txt to enumerate original file names, upload directory structures, and attachment slugs, undermining the plugin's file protection and potentially enabling direct file access if server-level restrictions are misconfigured or absent.

Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 are vulnerable to an uncontrolled resource consumption issue in Rex::Proto::Http::Request#normalize!. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send an HTTP request with a deeply nested path that triggers repeated rescans of the request target, causing quadratic CPU consumption and temporarily degrading the availability of any affected HTTP listener.

The issue is fixed in Metasploit Framework 6.5.10

NocoDB before 2026.10.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in passwordForgot() that allows unauthenticated attackers to revoke a user's sessions by requesting a password reset. Attackers who know a user's email can repeatedly request resets to sign out users, including super-admins, and permanently destroy their OAuth and MCP application authorizations.

Wallabag from 2.0.0-beta.1 before 2.6.16 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to annotate other users' entries by referencing global entry IDs. Attackers can send requests to the /annotations/{entry} or /api/annotations/{entry} routes to inject annotations into victims' private entries, API output, and exports, and enumerate existing entry IDs.

Cockpit CMS through 2.14.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with content create or update permission to inject script via unescaped linked item _id values. Attackers can save an item whose link _id contains a double quote and HTML markup, executing script when administrators view the content dashboard or collection list.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in BVHLoader.cpp that allows attackers to read freed aiNode objects because the mNodes vector is never cleared between files. Attackers can supply multiple BVH files to an application reusing one Importer instance, causing CreateAnimation to copy freed mName data into channel names, crashing the application or exposing heap contents.

Merchant for WooCommerce before 2.3.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Quick View module that allows unauthenticated attackers to read draft, pending, private, and scheduled WooCommerce products. The modal_content_ajax_callback() handler for the merchant_quick_view_content AJAX action is registered for unauthenticated users, is gated only by the merchant-nonce value exposed to every front-end visitor, and loads any supplied product_id with wc_get_product() without checking the product's post status or the user's read_post capability. Attackers can iterate product IDs to obtain the title, price, description, gallery images, and SKU of unpublished products when the Quick View module is enabled.

A security flaw has been discovered in hrshadhin CloudSchool up to 3.0.1. Affected is the function ReportController::marksheetPublic of the component Captcha Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument authorized_form results in improper authentication. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Astra WordPress theme before 4.14.0 contains an improper input neutralization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with contributor-level privileges to inject unescaped CSS by submitting a crafted overlay-opacity value in the ast-page-background-meta or ast-content-background-meta REST fields. Attackers can store a malicious payload that, when rendered, causes an uncaught TypeError leading to a fatal error and HTTP 500 denial of service on PHP 8.0+, or injects arbitrary CSS into the page's style block on PHP 7.x enabling UI redress and content spoofing.

SolarWinds Serv-U was found to be affected by an 
authentication vulnerability in its TOTP-based multi-factor authentication mechanism due to insufficient 
brute-force protection.

SolarWinds Serv-U was found to be affected by a 
username enumeration vulnerability allowing an attacker
to determine whether specific user accounts exist.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the STAP-A handling of gf_rtp_parse_h264 in rtp_depacketizer.c due to unchecked aggregation unit sizes. A malicious RTP sender or RTSP server can send STAP-A packets with oversized NAL unit lengths to disclose adjacent heap memory or crash the client.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_amr that allows remote RTP senders or malicious RTSP servers to read beyond packet buffers by sending crafted AMR/AMR-WB payloads. Attackers can send short packets whose TOC entries all set the F bit, causing out-of-bounds frame data to be copied into decoder output, disclosing memory or crashing the client.

UWAS before 0.11.16 contains a WAF bypass vulnerability in the isAPContentType() function within internal/middleware/security.go that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade SQL injection, XSS, and shell/RCE body pattern detection by setting the Content-Type header to application/json, multipart/form-data, or other exempted types. Attackers can relabel the Content-Type of malicious requests to skip WAF body scanning entirely, causing the unfiltered payload to pass through byte-for-byte to the backend application without being logged as a WAF event.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Webful Creations RepairBuddy computer-repair-shop allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects RepairBuddy: from n/a through 4.1237.

Canvas 7.0.0 before 7.2.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Contributors to inject scripts by exploiting a libxml2 parser differential in PostBody::clean(). Attackers can publish posts with slash-separated event handler attributes rendered unescaped in show.blade.php, hijacking Editor or Admin sessions to escalate their role to Admin.

Obtainium before 1.7.5 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows remote attackers to write or delete JSON files outside app_data by supplying an app id containing ../ sequences. Attackers can serve an obtainium://app deep link with a crafted id that, once imported, overwrites other app configurations or writes files to shared storage, and later deletes them on app removal.

Obtainium before 1.7.5 trusts the allowIdChange field in imported app data, allowing attackers to bypass the package ID mismatch check by delivering crafted obtainium://app deep links. Once a victim confirms the import, attackers can silently replace a tracked app with an attacker-controlled source and install a different APK, prompt-free when Shizuku or root is authorized.
