A maliciously crafted PDF file, when imported into Autodesk Revit, can trigger a Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause excessive memory consumption, potentially resulting in the application terminating unexpectedly.

A maliciously crafted PNG file, when imported into Autodesk Revit, can trigger a NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause the application to terminate unexpectedly, resulting in a denial-of-service.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.1 through 0.10.0, credentials are sent to a third party when a redirect's Location header hides the new host behind a backslash. A signed-in user who connects an MCP server URL, or runs a shared or marketplace workflow with a host-scoped credential, can have that credential delivered to a third party if the host responds with a redirect whose Location the other party influenced. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

A vulnerability has been found in javahuang SurveyKing up to 0.3.0-beta.3. Affected by this vulnerability is the function resolvePath of the file server/shared/src/main/java/cn/surveyking/server/storage/LocalStorageService.java of the component File Upload. Such manipulation of the argument basePath leads to path traversal. The attack can be launched remotely. The name of the patch is d469ef73d935ff64fd0cf603cf91b76877af02b6. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue.

A security flaw has been discovered in GongShengyue OnlineBooks up to dfc5eacc08d3b0396c266049548618f6fb9587ea. This issue affects the function listSplit of the file src/cn/ylcto/book/servlet/BooksServlet.java of the component BooksServlet. The manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

LiteLLM Secret Manager oidc Resolver Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of LiteLLM. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the secret resolution handler. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied input prior to using it to access environment variables. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-31482.

A vulnerability was determined in beenuar AiSOC up to 17.0.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the component AuditMiddleware. This manipulation causes improper verification of cryptographic signature. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 17.1.0 addresses this issue. Patch name: 8f2224299124010536ff0e3ebcd9efb0149af26c. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

A vulnerability has been found in louislam uptime-kuma up to e7420f8fa546a8baa7ac4bf9d10a32545d4346e0. Affected by this vulnerability is the function disableAPIKey/enableAPIKey of the file server/socket-handlers/api-key-socket-handler.js of the component API Key Management. The manipulation leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The researcher claims to have submitted a GHSA on the repository of the project.

A security flaw has been discovered in vanna-ai vanna 2.0.0/2.0.1/2.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is the function _load_index of the file src/vanna/integrations/faiss/agent_memory.py of the component FAISS AgentMemory Integration. Performing a manipulation results in deserialization. The attack needs to be approached locally. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. When processing log entries using certain JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) formatting templates, the service fails to properly escape input composed entirely of quotation marks or backslashes. An attacker who can supply logged input can exploit this issue to generate malformed JSON output, which may cause downstream log ingestion systems and parsers to reject log records.

A vulnerability was found in browser-use 0.13.13/0.13.14. This impacts the function load_and_migrate_config of the file browser_use/config.py of the component SecurityWatchdog. The manipulation results in improper authorization. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

LTplus-AG ifc-lite @ifc-lite/export before 4.13.1 and ifc-lite-export before 27.0.0 contain a STEP record injection vulnerability in the mutation writer via unescaped typed-value type names. Attackers controlling the mutations payload can place parentheses, semicolons, and newlines in typed.type to append arbitrary entity records to exported IFC files, bypassing the class-name guard.

WeKan before 12.78 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in Exporter.buildStream() that lets attackers retrieve checklists from other boards by supplying a checklistId export scope. Users able to export any board, or unauthenticated users via a public board, can read private checklists, their items and creator usernames even when anonymization is enabled.

WeKan before 12.78 contains an access control bypass in Exporter.buildCsvStream() that ignores the Disable all export and Anonymize export users settings. Board readers or unauthenticated users of public boards can request the CSV export endpoint to export all cards and reveal real usernames in member, assignee, and mention fields.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-useradmin/raw.cgi that allows attackers with LDAP attribute write access to inject markup. Attackers can store script in user or group attributes or the dn, which executes in an administrator's browser when viewing the raw entry.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mysql/view_table.cgi that allows MySQL users to inject scripts via unescaped column names. Attackers with CREATE or ALTER privilege can create columns containing HTML payloads that execute in a Webmin administrator's session when the table is viewed.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Servers Index module that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to inject scripts via the realhost field of UDP discovery replies. Attackers on the same broadcast domain can answer discovery scans with HTML or JavaScript stored by find_servers() and rendered unescaped by edit_serv.cgi, executing in Webmin user sessions.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-server/edit_browser.cgi that allows attackers with write access to LDAP entry attributes to inject script by storing markup in attribute values. When an administrator browses the entry in the LDAP Server directory browser, the unencoded script runs in the Webmin origin, letting attackers act with the administrator's session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject scripts by supplying values from managed hosts that cluster modules render unescaped. Attackers who can edit a Servers Index description, control a managed host, or intercept its RPC link can inject server descriptions, versions, user/group names, or package fields to execute JavaScript in the central administrator's session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Upload and Download module that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped HTTP status lines from background downloads. Attackers controlling a download server can return a malicious status line stored by updown/download.pl and printed unescaped by updown/index.cgi, executing script in a higher-privileged user's session.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ldap-client/popup_browser.cgi that allows attackers to inject markup by storing it in LDAP attribute values printed without HTML encoding. Attackers with write access to an LDAP directory entry, needing no Webmin account, can execute scripts in the Webmin origin when an administrator browses that entry.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows local users or directory writers to inject script by placing markup in user names, group names or GECOS fields. Attackers can set GECOS via chfn or modify LDAP, NIS or SSSD entries so unescaped values in my_user_chooser.cgi, my_group_chooser.cgi, user_chooser.cgi and group_chooser.cgi execute in a Webmin user's browser.
Reachable Assertion vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Walrus allows Input Data Manipulation.

A flaw has been found in Tenda RX3 16.03.13.11_multi. Affected by this vulnerability is the function fromSysToolRestoreSet of the file /goform/SysToolRestoreSet of the component httpd. Executing a manipulation can lead to missing authentication. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.

Open Babel through 3.2.1 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in OBForceField::Setup() that leaves stored constraints bound to freed atoms when set up with an empty molecule. Attackers can supply a molecule file yielding an empty molecule so later SteepestDescent() or ConjugateGradients() calls read freed memory, causing crashes or incorrect results.

Paid Memberships Pro before 3.8.8 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read restricted post excerpts because restriction is reapplied only through the_excerpt filter. Attackers can request RSS or Atom feeds, oEmbed URLs, or pages rendering the Post Excerpt block to read opening text or manual excerpts of member-only posts.

The MongoDB Rust driver's connection-string parser can include database password text and authentication property values in the error messages it returns when a connection string is malformed. The optional error-redaction feature does not fully remove this text. A party with read access to the application's logs or error output may obtain part or all of a database credential.

Jenkins Performance Plugin 1024.ve69e11844523 and earlier does not limit URL schemes for the external report links it creates based on Taurus XML format performance reports, allowing the `javascript:` scheme, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exploitable by attackers able to control these reports.

Jenkins Rich Text Publisher Plugin 1.5 and earlier does not escape job names in error messages rendered by the Rich Text Portlet, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exploitable by attackers with View/Configure permission.

An information exposure weakness in the connection string handling of the MongoDB Ruby Driver can place credential material from the application's own configuration into the text of a parsing error, where an existing redaction control does not apply. A party able to read the application's error output or logs may thereby obtain database credential text together with deployment coordinates. The condition arises entirely within the embedding application process and requires no database authentication.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a hardcoded cryptographic key vulnerability in the DHCAST128 login of the NSE afp.lua library, which uses a fixed, publicly known Diffie-Hellman private exponent. A passive observer of the network traffic between Nmap and an Apple Filing Protocol server can compute the shared secret from the hardcoded exponent and the server's public value and decrypt the password supplied to scripts such as afp-showmount.nse and afp-brute.nse through the afp.username and afp.password arguments, without man-in-the-middle access or cryptanalysis.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the inline AXFR response reader of the dns-zone-transfer.nse script, which reads the zone transfer response without a size limit. A malicious DNS server on a scanned host can stream unbounded data over TCP port 53 after the AXFR request, causing the memory of the Nmap process to grow at the attacker's send rate until it is exhausted.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the sendPacketsTCP function of the NSE dns.lua library, which reads a DNS-over-TCP response without a size limit and builds it by repeated string concatenation. A malicious DNS server on a scanned host can stream unbounded data in response to the initial SOA lookup made by dns-zone-transfer.nse, before any AXFR request is sent, causing unbounded memory growth and quadratic CPU cost in the Nmap process.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the negotiate_tn3270 function of the NSE tn3270.lua library, whose device-type search loop does not advance when the server sends a protocol-conformant DEVICETYPE IS response without an LU suffix. A TN3270E server on a scanned host, including a non-malicious one that sends such a response, causes a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process when tn3270-screen.nse runs, which the script-timeout option does not interrupt.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the process_write function of the NSE tn3270.lua library, whose write loop does not advance when it processes a malformed Repeat to Address (RA) order. A malicious TN3270 server on a scanned host can embed a single 6-byte malformed RA order in an ordinary screen-write data stream after a normal negotiation, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process when tn3270-screen.nse runs, which the script-timeout option does not interrupt.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the dispatcher of the NSE tftp.lua library, which removes completed coroutines but not ones that ended in an error, leaving a zero-yield spin. A malicious TFTP exchange reached by snmp-ios-config.nse after an SNMP write sequence can leave a dead coroutine that freezes the entire Nmap invocation, before port scanning begins for any target in the run; the hang is prevented when the script-timeout option is set.

Leptonica 1.79.0 through 1.87.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in l_byteaInitFromStream() that allows attackers to write past a heap buffer by supplying oversized input. Attackers can provide a file larger than 1,000,000,000 bytes, causing l_byteaCreate() to allocate a 201-byte buffer before memcpy copies the full stream size, crashing the application.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the Bandwidth SMS webhook endpoint POST /webhooks/sms/:phone_number that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit forged SMS events. Attackers who know an inbox phone number can set the 'to' field to inject inbound messages with forged sender numbers or forge delivery status updates.

Loginizer before 2.1.4 contains a brute-force lockout bypass vulnerability in loginizer_login_failed() that allows unauthenticated attackers to avoid failed-attempt recording via non-ASCII URL bytes. Attackers can append invalid UTF-8 or 4-byte sequences to wp-login.php or xmlrpc.php request URLs, causing the log INSERT to fail and enabling unlimited password guessing without lockout or email notification.

GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmlValidatePopElement because xmlCtxtReset frees the DTD without popping stale validation states. Attackers supplying an XML document ending inside an element to an application reusing a DTD-validating xmlTextReader can trigger heap reads, causing crashes and limited heap disclosure via error messages.

GEOS 3.13.0 before 3.15.1 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in RectangleContains::isContainedInBoundary that recurses indefinitely on curved geometries returned by getGeometryN. Attackers can supply crafted WKT or WKB CircularString, CompoundCurve, or CurvePolygon geometries tested via PreparedGeometry::contains or GEOSPreparedContains against a prepared rectangle to crash the process with a stack overflow.

GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger stale DTD validation states after xmlTextReaderCurrentDoc documents are freed. Attackers can supply an XML document ending with an error inside an element, causing xmlTextReaderClose to read freed element declarations, leading to crashes and possible invalid frees.

OpenCV 3.0.0 through 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 through 5.1.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the built-in MJPEG encoder when writing grayscale frames due to incorrect level shifting in convertToYUV(). Attackers controlling pixel content written as grayscale MJPEG video can trigger unchecked cat_table and huff_dc_tab lookups, leaking adjacent or uninitialized memory into the output file or crashing the process.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 14.4 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to cause denial of service due to unconstrained backtracking in regular expression evaluation.

A vulnerability was determined in FastStone Image Viewer up to 8.5. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file FSViewer.exe of the component ICO Decoder. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds write. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. The affected element is the function getLanguageContent of the file src/EditorsHandlers/ContentTools.php of the component ContentTools Editor. This manipulation of the argument ContentToolsUrl causes server-side request forgery. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager with access to two advertisers can associate a conversion tracker owned by one advertiser with a campaign owned by the other. The tracker-campaign page checks access to each object but does not verify that their actual owners match. The resulting association can expose the first advertiser's tracker name and identifier in the second advertiser's restricted conversion report.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the public conversion-variable endpoint does not verify that a caller-supplied conversion belongs to the supplied tracker. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a unique variable for a different tracker's conversion, causing that conversion to be classified as a duplicate and excluded from conversion reports.

A vulnerability was identified in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file admin/partials/user_logged.php. The manipulation leads to missing authorization. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

The ShopMagic – email automation for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.5 Although `CurrentCustomer::encode_tracking_data()` appends an md5 hash to the `shopmagic_visitor_<COOKIEHASH>` cookie to make it tamper-resistant, `CookiePersistence::get_tracking_data()` returns the raw `json_decode()`'d cookie value directly without computing or verifying that hash, leaving the cookie's `user_id`, `email`, and `meta` fields fully under attacker control. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to forge the visitor cookie — which is predictable because its name is derived as `md5(siteurl)` from the public site URL — and submit it to the unprotected `wp_ajax_nopriv_capture_email_url` endpoint (which is registered without a nonce check or capability check) to impersonate any WordPress user including administrators in ShopMagic's customer-identity context, and to overwrite the stored profile metadata — including name, phone number, and billing address — of any existing guest record in `wp_shopmagic_guest` and `wp_shopmagic_guest_meta` via `GuestManager::save()`.

The CubeWP Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.32 This is due to the `cubewp_frontend_role_caps()` function, registered on the `user_has_cap` filter, which excludes REST API requests via a `REST_REQUEST` guard but omits a corresponding `XMLRPC_REQUEST` check, causing it to unconditionally widen capabilities for any Subscriber or Contributor on XML-RPC and admin-ajax.php request paths. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to the full Contributor role capability set — gaining `edit_posts`, `delete_posts`, and `read` — allowing them to create, edit, and delete posts through core XML-RPC methods such as `wp.newPost`. Critically, the capability widening is not scoped to CubeWP's own submission handlers but applies globally to all core capability gates on affected request paths, meaning any Subscriber account can exploit this with a single standard XML-RPC call and no CubeWP-specific interaction. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive every capability defined for the Contributor role.

A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the udevConnectListAllInterfaces() function in libvirt. This issue can occur when detaching a host interface while at the same time collecting the list of interfaces via virConnectListAllInterfaces API. This flaw could be used to perform a denial of service attack by causing the libvirt daemon to crash.
A flaw has been discovered in GnuTLS where an application crash can be induced when attempting to verify a specially crafted .pem bundle using the "certtool --verify-chain" command.

A flaw was found in the 389-ds-base LDAP Server. This issue occurs when issuing a Modify DN LDAP operation through the ldap protocol, when the function return value is not tested and a NULL pointer is dereferenced. If a privileged user performs a ldap MODDN operation after a failed operation, it could lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) or system crash.

A flaw was found in GLib, which is vulnerable to an integer overflow in the g_string_insert_unichar() function. When the position at which to insert the character is large, the position will overflow, leading to a buffer underwrite.

A flaw was found in Samba. The smbd service daemon does not pick up group membership changes when re-authenticating an expired SMB session. This issue can expose file shares until clients disconnect and then connect again.

A flaw was found in libssh versions built with OpenSSL versions older than 3.0, specifically in the ssh_kdf() function responsible for key derivation. Due to inconsistent interpretation of return values where OpenSSL uses 0 to indicate failure and libssh uses 0 for success—the function may mistakenly return a success status even when key derivation fails. This results in uninitialized cryptographic key buffers being used in subsequent communication, potentially compromising SSH sessions' confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

A vulnerability has been identified in the GRUB2 bootloader's network module that poses an immediate Denial of Service (DoS) risk. This flaw is a Use-after-Free issue, caused because the net_set_vlan command is not properly unregistered when the network module is unloaded from memory. An attacker who can execute this command can force the system to access memory locations that are no longer valid. Successful exploitation leads directly to system instability, which can result in a complete crash and halt system availability

A use-after-free vulnerability has been identified in the GNU GRUB (Grand Unified Bootloader). The flaw occurs because the file-closing process incorrectly retains a memory pointer, leaving an invalid reference to a file system structure. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause grub to crash, leading to a Denial of Service. Possible data integrity or confidentiality compromise is not discarded.

A vulnerability has been identified in the GRUB2 bootloader's normal command that poses an immediate Denial of Service (DoS) risk. This flaw is a Use-after-Free issue, caused because the normal command is not properly unregistered when the module is unloaded. An attacker who can execute this command can force the system to access memory locations that are no longer valid. Successful exploitation leads directly to system instability, which can result in a complete crash and halt system availability. Impact on the data integrity and confidentiality is also not discarded.

A vulnerability in the GRUB2 bootloader has been identified in the normal module. This flaw, a memory Use After Free issue, occurs because the normal_exit command is not properly unregistered when its related module is unloaded. An attacker can exploit this condition by invoking the command after the module has been removed, causing the system to improperly access a previously freed memory location. This leads to a system crash or possible impacts in data confidentiality and integrity.

A flaw was found in QEMU. A specially crafted VMDK image could trigger an out-of-bounds read vulnerability, potentially leading to a 12-byte leak of sensitive information or a denial of service condition (DoS).

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An administrator with `manage-users` permission can bypass the "Only administrators can view" setting for unmanaged attributes, allowing them to modify these attributes. This improper access control can lead to unauthorized changes to user profiles, even when the system is configured to restrict such modifications.

An incomplete fix for CVE-2024-47778 allows an out-of-bounds read in gst_wavparse_adtl_chunk() function. The patch added a size validation check lsize + 8 > size, but it does not account for the GST_ROUND_UP_2(lsize) used in the actual offset calculation. When lsize is an odd number, the parser advances more bytes than validated, causing OOB read.

A flaw was found in GIMP. A stack buffer overflow vulnerability in the TIM image loader's 4BPP decoding path allows a local user to cause a Denial of Service (DoS). By opening a specially crafted TIM image file, the application crashes due to an unconditional overflow when writing to a variable-length array.

A flaw was found in GIMP. This vulnerability, a heap buffer over-read in the `icns_slurp()` function, occurs when processing specially crafted ICNS image files. An attacker could provide a malicious ICNS file, potentially leading to application crashes or information disclosure on systems that process such files.

A flaw was found in binutils, specifically within the `readelf` utility. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by tricking a user into processing a specially crafted Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) file. The exploitation of this flaw can lead to the system becoming unresponsive due to excessive resource consumption or a program crash.
The web administration panel binds broadly to the public IPv6 address space on port [::]:8080 without default firewall limits, making internal API endpoints reachable over the WAN.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. The ldap_utf8prev() function reads bytes before the start of a buffer without bounds checking, causing a heap buffer over-read in string filter parsing that may influence internal filter processing behavior.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. The SMD5 password storage plugin performs unsigned integer underflow when computing salt length from a crafted password hash shorter than 16 bytes, causing a buffer over-read that crashes the LDAP server during authentication.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. The PBKDF2-SHA256 password storage plugin does not enforce an upper bound on the iteration count extracted from stored password hashes. A privileged attacker who can modify a user's password hash can cause excessive CPU consumption during authentication, resulting in denial of service.

A stack buffer overflow flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. The checkPrefix() function in pw.c copies an attacker-controlled algorithm ID into a 256-byte stack buffer without bounds checking when parsing reversible-encrypted attribute values. An attacker with Directory Manager privileges can crash the LDAP server by storing a crafted credential with an oversized algorithm ID. FORTIFY_SOURCE mitigates this to denial of service only.

An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5 in the berval2tl_data() function in plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c. The function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2) without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated to uint16_t, yielding 0xFFFE (65534) or 0xFFFF (65535). The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to 65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read.
The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or kadmind reads principal data.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. During schema reload, the attr_syntax_swap_ht() function unconditionally frees attribute syntax information nodes, bypassing the refcount-based deferred deletion used elsewhere in the attribute syntax subsystem. If an administrator triggers schema reload while concurrent LDAP query traffic is active, worker threads may access freed memory, resulting in use-after-free or double-free and a denial of service (server crash).

A flaw was found in spice-vdagent. A malicious or compromised SPICE host can trigger an integer overflow by sending a specially crafted message. This vulnerability can lead to a heap buffer overflow, causing the spice-vdagent daemon to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the virtual machine. This issue requires the SPICE host to be untrusted or compromised for exploitation.

A flaw was found in dhcp-server. A remote attacker with network access to the OMAPI (Open Management Application Programming Interface) port, especially if not secured with TSIG (Transaction Signature) key authentication, could send a specially crafted lease creation request. This request, containing an overly long InfiniBand MAC address, triggers a buffer overflow in the `print_hw_addr()` function. Successful exploitation leads to a persistent denial of service (DoS), causing the `dhcpd` service to crash and preventing it from restarting without manual intervention.

A flaw was found in luksmeta. A local attacker with administrative privileges can cause data corruption when saving metadata to a Linux Unified Key Setup (LUKS) device. Due to incorrect boundary calculations and flawed overlap detection, new metadata entries can be written beyond available free space or over existing records. This issue can corrupt stored encrypted payload data or existing metadata, potentially rendering the affected data inaccessible.
Out-of-bounds read in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

A flaw was found in cockpit-machines. Red Hat Subscription Management (RHSM) authentication tokens are passed as command-line arguments to background helper processes during image retrieval operations. A local, unprivileged attacker on a system permitting cross-user process inspection can view these arguments while the process is active. This flaw can lead to information disclosure, potentially allowing unauthorized access to RHSM resources within the token's validity period.

A flaw was found in cockpit-machines. When saving Virtual Network Computing (VNC) console settings, the configured password is passed directly as a command-line argument to an underlying system utility. A local unprivileged attacker on a host that allows cross-user process inspection could read the exposed password from the process list while another user modifies settings. This credential disclosure can allow unauthorized access to the guest virtual machine's graphical console.

A flaw was found in device-mapper-multipath. A local user can trigger an out-of-bounds read by sending a command with a format string ending in a trailing percent character to the multipath daemon. This issue can allow the user to expose unintended daemon memory, leading to information disclosure, or cause the daemon to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A high privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

Pika before 1.5.0 contains an uncontrolled resource allocation vulnerability that allows malicious brokers to exhaust client memory by declaring oversized frame payloads. In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user could trick a user that holds a role with the ueba_can_view_ui capability into opening a link that the unauthenticated user creates for the User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Overview dashboard. When the user opens the link, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opens the link. The commands could expose or modify some data available to the user who opens the link and partially disrupt search processing.
The vulnerability is possible because the User and Entity Behavior Analytics Overview dashboard does not escape dashboard filter values from the link before substituting the values into SPL searches.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see UEBA dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.8/analytics/ueba-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

Description

`CookieConverter.getCookies` decides which stored cookies to attach to an outbound request. The
applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Domain` attribute, so a cookie
without one, which is the ordinary form of a session cookie, skips scoping entirely and is returned for
whatever target URL was passed. RFC 6265 requires the opposite: a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is
host-only and belongs to the host that set it.

Two further defects sit in the same method. The domain comparison has no notion of a registrable
domain, so a `Domain` value of `com` matches every host under it, and the comparison returns true when
it throws, so a failure to evaluate the check admits the cookie. Neither the converter nor
`MetadataTransfer`, which carries the stored cookie to outlinks, ever considers the host that issued
it.

Cookie handling is opt-in: it requires `http.use.cookies` to be set to true, which is not the default,
and the cookie key to be listed in `metadata.transfer`. The documented recipe does not work as written,
because the `metadata.transfer` example in the internals documentation names `set-cookie` while the key
present in metadata is `protocol.set-cookie` and the transfer matches key names exactly. Deployments
affected are therefore those where an operator determined the correct key, enabled cookie handling and
crawls an authenticated site whose pages link or redirect to other hosts. In that case the session
cookie of the authenticated origin is sent to those hosts.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a cookie without a `Domain` attribute is sent only to the host that set it, a
single-label domain is rejected and the domain check fails closed. Because the protocol does not yet
record the host that issued a cookie, cookies without a `Domain` attribute are not sent at all until
that host is recorded; operators relying on cookie transfer will notice this. The documentation error
is corrected in the same release.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should confine an authenticated crawl to a topology whose URL
filters keep it on the origin that issued the credentials, and should not rely on cookie scoping as a
boundary. Rotating session credentials used for such crawls is advisable.

Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept.

Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated
and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database
password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own
redaction masks it as PWD=xxxxx:

- Pressing "Test" in the Windows data source setup dialog (psqlsetup.dll)
  logs the whole connection string, which carries PWD= percent-encoded,
  which is reversible, and any password= or sslpassword= inside pqopt.
- The Unicode connect functions SQLDriverConnectW, SQLConnectW and
  SQLBrowseConnectW log their arguments as they convert them between UTF-16
  and UTF-8, before the masking happens. The ANSI entry points are unaffected.

Turning the log on takes an administrator, and MyLog is off by default. The
exposure is the person who later reads the log, which in practice means a log
attached to a bug report or handed to support. Making that safe is the purpose
of the driver's redaction, and these two sites bypassed it.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A security flaw has been discovered in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. Affected by this issue is the function plugins.set_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Performing a manipulation results in null pointer dereference. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A weakness has been identified in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This affects the function wg-client.add_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Executing a manipulation can lead to null pointer dereference. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. You should upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A security vulnerability has been detected in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This vulnerability affects the function wg-client.set_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. The manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. The attack can be initiated remotely. The affected component should be upgraded. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A vulnerability has been found in TAILG Feimeng up to 20261028. Affected is an unknown function of the component Wireless Remote Control System. The manipulation leads to authentication bypass by capture-replay. The attack needs to be initiated within the local network. The attack is considered to have high complexity. The exploitability is told to be difficult. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

wpa_supplicant 2.7 through 2.12 with the wolfSSL backend contains an EAP-FAST server authentication bypass in tls_sess_sec_cb() that skips master secret derivation for oversized PAC-Opaque tickets. Adjacent attackers running a rogue authenticator can complete the handshake with an all-zero master secret to capture MS-CHAPv2 responses for offline cracking and replace the stored PAC.

A use-after-free flaw was found in the xorg-x11-server. An X server crash may occur in a very specific and legacy configuration (a multi-screen setup with multiple protocol screens, also known as Zaphod mode) if the pointer is warped from within a window on one screen to the root window of the other screen and if the original window is destroyed followed by another window being destroyed.

A null pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel API for the cryptographic algorithm scatterwalk functionality. This issue occurs when a user constructs a malicious packet with specific socket configuration, which could allow a local user to crash the system or escalate their privileges on the system.

A heap use-after-free issue has been identified in SQLite in the jsonParseAddNodeArray() function in sqlite3.c. This flaw allows a local attacker to leverage a victim to pass specially crafted malicious input to the application, potentially causing a crash and leading to a denial of service.

A vulnerability exists in the bind-propagation option of the Dockerfile RUN --mount instruction. The system does not properly validate the input passed to this option, allowing users to pass arbitrary parameters to the mount instruction. This issue can be exploited to mount sensitive directories from the host into a container during the build process and, in some cases, modify the contents of those mounted files. Even if SELinux is used, this vulnerability can bypass its protection by allowing the source directory to be relabeled to give the container access to host files.

A vulnerability was found in PAM. The secret information is stored in memory, where the attacker can trigger the victim program to execute by sending characters to its standard input (stdin). As this occurs, the attacker can train the branch predictor to execute an ROP chain speculatively. This flaw could result in leaked passwords, such as those found in /etc/shadow while performing authentications.

A vulnerability was found in systemd-coredump. This flaw allows an attacker to force a SUID process to crash and replace it with a non-SUID binary to access the original's privileged process coredump, allowing the attacker to read sensitive data, such as /etc/shadow content, loaded by the original process.

A SUID binary or process has a special type of permission, which allows the process to run with the file owner's permissions, regardless of the user executing the binary. This allows the process to access more restricted data than unprivileged users or processes would be able to. An attacker can leverage this flaw by forcing a SUID process to crash and force the Linux kernel to recycle the process PID before systemd-coredump can analyze the /proc/pid/auxv file. If the attacker wins the race condition, they gain access to the original's SUID process coredump file. They can read sensitive content loaded into memory by the original binary, affecting data confidentiality.

A flaw was found in libssh, a library that implements the SSH protocol. When calculating the session ID during the key exchange (KEX) process, an allocation failure in cryptographic functions may lead to a NULL pointer dereference. This issue can cause the client or server to crash.

There's a vulnerability in the libssh package where when a libssh consumer passes in an unexpectedly large input buffer to ssh_get_fingerprint_hash() function. In such cases the bin_to_base64() function can experience an integer overflow leading to a memory under allocation, when that happens it's possible that the program perform out of bounds write leading to a heap corruption.
This issue affects only 32-bits builds of libssh.
glib-networking's OpenSSL backend fails to properly check the return value of a call to BIO_write(), resulting in an out of bounds read.

A vulnerability has been identified in the GRUB (Grand Unified Bootloader) component. This flaw occurs because the bootloader mishandles string conversion when reading information from a USB device, allowing an attacker to exploit inconsistent length values. A local attacker can connect a maliciously configured USB device during the boot sequence to trigger this issue. A successful exploitation may lead GRUB to crash, leading to a Denial of Service. Data corruption may be also possible, although given the complexity of the exploit the impact is most likely limited.

A flaw was found in libnbd. A malicious actor could exploit this by convincing libnbd to open a specially crafted Uniform Resource Identifier (URI). This vulnerability arises because non-standard hostnames starting with '-o' are incorrectly interpreted as arguments to the Secure Shell (SSH) process, rather than as hostnames. This could lead to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running libnbd.

A flaw was found in libsoup’s WebSocket frame processing when handling incoming messages. If a non-default configuration is used where the maximum incoming payload size is unset, the library may read memory outside the intended bounds. This can cause unintended memory exposure or a crash. Applications using libsoup’s WebSocket support with this configuration may be impacted.

An API design flaw in WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit allows untrusted web content to unexpectedly perform IP connections, DNS lookups, and HTTP requests. Applications expect to use the
WebPage::send-request signal handler to approve or reject all network requests. However, certain types of HTTP requests bypass this signal handler.

A flaw was found in libsoup. A remote attacker could exploit an unsigned to signed conversion error in the `soup_body_input_stream_read_chunked()` function by sending a malicious HTTP request. This vulnerability occurs when libsoup operates behind a non-libsoup proxy server or as a proxy in front of a non-libsoup backend server. Successful exploitation can allow an attacker to bypass security controls, poison web caches, or gain unauthorized access.

A flaw was found in vLLM, an open-source library for large language model inference. This vulnerability arises from improper handling of image metadata, specifically EXIF orientation and PNG transparency (tRNS) data, during image processing. When images are converted to RGB, transparency information may be implicitly discarded or remapped, leading to unexpected rendering of transparent pixels and distortion of input content. This can result in the model misinterpreting image content, potentially affecting the integrity of processed data.

The fix for CVE-2026-2443 was regressed by a subsequent rework commit that replaced specific overflow checks with a general signed comparison. When a client sends a Range request with a suffix length exceeding the content size, the resulting negative start value is not properly clamped, leading to malformed HTTP 206 responses and log flooding.

The fix for CVE-2026-0716 (commit 6ff7ef0, libsoup 3.6.6) placed the integer overflow guard inside the if (masked) block, leaving unmasked server-to-client frames unprotected. A malicious WebSocket server can send a crafted unmasked frame with a payload length near UINT64_MAX to trigger an OOB read in a libsoup-based client when max_incoming_payload_size is set to 0.

A vulnerability was found in the internal Access Control List (ACL) subsystem of kronosnet (Version affected: <= 1.34). When the framework is explicitly configured to manage dynamic links (accepting network traffic from any IP address) without network payload encryption, the validation architecture implicitly trusts the link ID provided within incoming data packets. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this lack of validation by spoofing a legitimate link ID inside crafted network frames. This allows the attacker to fully bypass the ACL framework and inject arbitrary data packets into the application layer, potentially leading to data corruption or service instabilities.

A path traversal flaw was found in WildFly's domain mode
  implementation. The LocalFileRepository.getFile() and
  getConfigurationFile() methods in
  wildfly-core/deployment-repository do not validate that the
  resolved file path remains within the configured repository or
  configuration root directories. A remote attacker who has
  obtained the slave host controller secret or compromised a slave
  host controller can supply a crafted relative path containing
  directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../../etc/passwd) via the
  slave-DC wire protocol, causing the Domain Controller to resolve
  and serve arbitrary files readable by the DC process. This leads
  to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information such as
  configuration files, keystores, and system credentials.

A flaw was found in gdk-pixbuf. When loading a specially crafted JPEG image containing chunked ICC profile markers, an error during ICC profile parsing can leave stale size metadata after the profile buffer is freed. A subsequent allocation in the same decode can cause an out-of-bounds write, potentially crashing the application. To exploit this flaw, an application using gdk-pixbuf must process the malicious JPEG image.

Affected version >= 2.26.4

A stack overflow vulnerability was found in gfs2-utils. The hash table traversal code in metawalk.c uses alloca() with an exponentially-derived size from the untrusted on-disk di_depth field without bounds validation. A crafted GFS2 filesystem image with a large di_depth value causes stack exhaustion and a denial of service when processed by fsck.gfs2, gfs2_edit, or savemeta.

A stack overflow vulnerability was found in gfs2-utils. The metadata walk code in metawalk.c uses alloca() with an untrusted inode height value from on-disk metadata without bounds validation, causing stack exhaustion and a denial of service when processing crafted GFS2 filesystem images.

A flaw was found in the buildah/copier Go package. When used outside of Buildah by a non-root caller, a crafted tar archive containing malicious symlinks can escape the target extraction directory and create files outside the intended destination. Buildah itself uses chroot hardening and is not affected.

U-Boot versions 2025.04 before 2026.10-rc3 contain an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in read_slotted_partition() that fails to validate image size against partition bounds. Attackers with physical access can supply crafted boot media with oversized headers to write past the load buffer into bootloader memory on devices without Android Verified Boot protection.

A flaw was found in SSSD. A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the Kerberos Credential Manager (KCM) responder during Kerberos ticket-granting ticket (TGT) renewal, where a deferred callback accesses memory that has already been released. An authenticated local user with a renewable Kerberos ticket can trigger this issue on systems configured with KCM renewal, causing the KCM responder service to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in SSSD. A local user can cause a denial of service (DoS) by disrupting system authentication services. When handling Generic Security Services Application Programming Interface (GSSAPI) authentication in the Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) responder, cached connection state is freed upon completion without clearing the reference pointer. An attacker can exploit this by sending an additional request over the same connection, causing the service to access invalid memory and unexpectedly terminate.

A flaw was found in sssd. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting the responder service's available file descriptors (system handles used for open connections). By opening and maintaining many concurrent connections to a responder socket while continuing to queue new connection attempts, an attacker can trigger an unthrottled retry loop. This condition leads to high CPU utilization and stalls the service, preventing legitimate identity and authentication requests from being processed.

A flaw was found in SSSD. A local user can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by exploiting a race condition in the autofs responder between asynchronous enumeration completion and map invalidation. By repeatedly sending concurrent map enumeration and invalidation requests, an attacker can cause memory to leak, leading to excessive memory consumption that can disrupt or crash the autofs service.

A flaw was found in the clevis PKCS#11 pin. The clevis-pkcs11-afunix-socket-unlock daemon crashes when an AF_UNIX client connects to the data socket without a bound address, due to an integer underflow in the getpeername result handling. This causes a denial of service, preventing LUKS disk decryption from completing during boot.

A flaw was found in the clevis PKCS#11 pin. The clevis-pkcs11-afunix-socket-unlock daemon creates AF_UNIX sockets without explicit permission restrictions or peer credential verification. Under a permissive process umask, any local user can connect to the control socket and inject arbitrary device/key pairs, or connect to the data socket to receive LUKS passphrases.

A flaw was found in the clevis PKCS#11 pin. The clevis-luks-pkcs11-askpin script writes the PKCS#11 token PIN in plaintext to a file without setting restrictive permissions. Under the default process umask, the file is world-readable. Additionally, the PIN file is not reliably cleaned up if the decryption script exits early, leaving the PIN accessible indefinitely.

A flaw was found in the clevis PKCS#11 pin. The clevis-decrypt-pkcs11 script passes the PKCS#11 token PIN as a command-line argument to pkcs11-tool, making it visible to any local user through process listing or the /proc filesystem.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Motion Pixels decoder because mp_decode_frame() ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers supplying a roughly 2^28-byte packet through the libavcodec API overflow the bit count, causing reads from a NULL buffer that crash the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavcodec/jvdec.c that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying oversized JV video packets. Attackers can pass a roughly 268435460-byte packet through the libavcodec API, overflowing the bit count so decode_frame() reads from a NULL buffer and causes denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in mp_decode_frame() in libavcodec/mpegaudiodec_template.c because init_get_bits() failure is ignored after a signed integer overflow. Attackers can pass an oversized packet to the mp3adu decoder through the libavcodec API, causing reads through a NULL buffer that crash the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the dts2pts bitstream filter that allows attackers to exhaust CPU through unbounded per-packet POC node allocation. Attackers can supply a crafted H.264 packet with many slices of alternating picture order counts, forcing h264_queue_frame() to allocate tree nodes per slice and deny service.

FFmpeg 8.1 through 9.0.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the lcevc_metadata bitstream filter caused by a process block position mismatch in lcevc_metadata_handle_vui(). Attackers can supply crafted LCEVC access units with two IDR or non-IDR NAL units to trigger an av_assert0 failure in ff_cbs_lcevc_list_add(), aborting the application.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a reference count leak in libavcodec/v4l2_buffers.c that allows attackers to deadlock the V4L2 mem2mem decoder on multi-plane capture formats. Attackers can supply crafted H.264, HEVC, or VP9 streams with resolution changes, making ff_v4l2_m2m_codec_reinit() wait forever and hang the decoding application.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a division by zero vulnerability in dovi_configure_ext() in libavcodec/dovi_rpuenc.c that allows attackers to crash the process via an unvalidated frame rate denominator. Attackers can supply a crafted HEVC or AV1 input with a nonzero frame rate numerator and zero denominator to the dovi_rpu bitstream filter or libx265, libaom, or libsvtav1 encoders, causing denial of service.

FFmpeg 9.0 through 9.0.2 built with liblcevc_dec fails to validate LCEVC enhanced output dimensions against max_pixels in libavcodec/decode.c before frame allocation. Attackers can supply crafted H.264, HEVC or VVC streams declaring huge LCEVC resolutions to force oversized get_buffer2() allocations and exhaust memory.
Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
Concurrent execution using shared resource with improper synchronization ('race condition') in Windows Installer allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.
Buffer over-read in Windows USB Video Driver allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.
Use of uninitialized resource in Windows Graphics Kernel allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.
Out-of-bounds read in Windows Kernel allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information with a physical attack.

react-native-webview 13.8.0 through 17.1.0 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by placing unescaped backticks or ${} sequences in injectedJavaScriptObject string values. Attackers who control values like profile fields or API responses can break out of the template literal to access the page DOM, non-HttpOnly cookies, and the ReactNativeWebView message bridge.

agentic-radar 0.7.0 before 0.14.2 contains an untrusted configuration loading vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to inject environment variables by having load_dotenv() in agentic_radar/cli.py load the scanned repository's .env file. Attackers can set OPENAI_BASE_URL to an attacker-controlled host so that scan openai-agents or --harden-prompts send requests carrying the user's OpenAI API key to the attacker.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the cross_sell_group_name parameter in admin/cross_sell_groups.php. Attackers with per-page access to cross-selling groups can store a script payload that executes in other administrators' browsers, including full administrators, when they view the group listing.
Dell PowerStore contains a CSV Injection vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to code execution on another user's workstation.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.
PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V 1.1 is vulnerable to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in admin/search-invoices.php via the searchdata parameter.

SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup reference names in MediaWiki:Smw_allows_pattern. Once an editor annotates the matching Allows pattern value, AllowsPatternValue emits it unescaped on Special:Browse, executing JavaScript in every viewer's session.

A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in SSH key management was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the queued build Overview tab was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the Pull Requests branch filter health report was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the unknown VCS root page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the Slack Notifier settings page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS on the Versioned Settings page was possible

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie builds the match regular expression for each path-scoped middleware from its mount path without collapsing duplicate slashes, even when the application enables the ignoreDuplicateSlashes router option. Under that option Fastify's router collapses duplicate slashes in both the registered route and the request path, so a mount path containing a doubled slash is served by the router at its single-slash form while the middleware's compiled match still requires the doubled slash and never matches. A path-scoped middleware such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is therefore skipped while the router dispatches the request to the protected handler, without any authentication required. Applications are affected when they enable ignoreDuplicateSlashes and a middleware mount path reaches middie with a duplicate slash, most commonly when a plugin prefix that ends with a slash is joined to a mount path that starts with one. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid mount paths and plugin prefixes that introduce duplicate slashes.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient sanitization of objective identifiers in the SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) objectives report allows an authenticated user with content upload permissions to inject malicious scripts. When another user views the report, the injected script executes in their browser session, potentially allowing the attacker to access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows administrators with product editing permission to inject script via the products_name field. The unescaped name is rendered in the h1 heading of product detail and reviews pages, executing script in the browsers of shoppers and logged-in customers.

A weakness in the MongoDB Node.js driver can place sensitive information taken from an application-supplied connection string into the text of an error produced while that connection string is being parsed. The error is generated inside the application process before any database connection is made, so no database account and no network access are needed for it to occur. A party able to read the application's error output or log files may thereby obtain database credentials that the application's configuration source would otherwise keep to a narrower audience.

The MongoDB Go driver's connection string parser includes the raw, undecoded value of a query option in the error it returns when that value contains invalid percent encodings. When the option holds a secret, such as a TLS key file password or an AWS session token, the secret appears in plain text in the error. A party with low-privileged read access to wherever the application records or displays that error may learn the secret.

A MongoDB C# Driver component that interprets connection configuration supplied by the hosting application can include the caller-supplied configuration value in the text of the error it raises when that value cannot be interpreted. The redaction applied to that text does not cover all forms in which secret material may appear, so authentication material embedded in the configuration value can be preserved in the resulting error text and in anything that records it. Exploitation requires only the low privilege needed to observe the application's own error output or logs on the system where the driver runs; no database credentials or server connectivity are required. The result is disclosure of sensitive information to parties whose access to error output is broader than their intended access to the configuration secret.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject malicious content into a Splunk Web view. When another authenticated user opens the affected view in Splunk Web, the injected content executes unauthorized JavaScript code within the viewing user's browser session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not properly validate content in a view definition before rendering the view.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data that populates the Malware Activity report. Another user with access to the report could later click a related row. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who clicked the row. The commands could access data and perform actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Malware Activity report does not treat values from the Malware data model as literal search values when it builds drilldown searches.
For more information see Malware Activity (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/malware-activity) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the edit_timeline capability could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a legacy investigation timeline entry. Another user that holds a role with the manage_all_investigations capability could later open the investigation and select Run Search from the timeline. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run the SPL stored by the first user using the permissions of the user who selected Run Search. The SPL stored by the first user could access data or perform actions available to the user who selected Run Search.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not treat stored investigation search content as a literal search before building the Search page link.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.3/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Add details to an investigation in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-7/user-guide/7.3/investigations/add-details-to-an-investigation-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data that populates the System Misconfigurations report. Another user with access to the report could later select a related row. The System Misconfigurations report could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the row. The commands could access or modify data available to the user who selected the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Misconfigurations report does not treat values from the Vulnerabilities data model as literal search values when it builds drilldown searches.
For more information see System Misconfigurations (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/system-misconfigurations) and Configure users and roles (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-the-app/configure-users-and-roles) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in intrusion detection data. Another user who holds the "pci_user" role could later select the corresponding row in the Intrusion Detection and Prevention System Alert Activity Details panel. The report could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the row. The commands could access data and perform actions available to the user who selected the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Intrusion Detection and Prevention System Alert Activity report does not treat intrusion detection values as literal search values when it builds the details drilldown search.
For more information see Reports (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/user-manual/8.7/using-the-splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/reports) and Configure users and roles (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-the-app/configure-users-and-roles) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in data used by the Credit Card Data Found dashboard. If another user who can access the dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Credit Card Data Found dashboard does not validate source and destination values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Credit Card Data Found (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/credit-card-data-found) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise for Windows versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user that holds a role with the edit_user capability could create multiple user accounts that share the same user directory. This could expose user-specific configuration between those accounts, let one account modify configuration used by another account, or disrupt features that depend on separate user directories.
The vulnerability is caused by improper validation of usernames before Splunk Enterprise performs Windows filesystem operations. Windows removes trailing periods from directory names, so distinct usernames can resolve to the same user directory.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.0, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared data model calculation. When a user who can run a search against the shared data model runs one, the injected SPL can run using the permissions of the user who ran the search. This could expose sensitive credentials to the user who created the shared data model.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not safely neutralize data model calculation fields before it includes them in generated searches.
For more information see About data models (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/build-a-data-model/about-data-models) in the Splunk documentation.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

A component of the MongoDB Java Driver that processes connection configuration places credential values taken from that configuration into generated text and error output without replacing them with a placeholder, unlike other parts of the driver. A party able to read output produced by an application that embeds the driver may obtain database or proxy credentials in clear text.

The Okta Client SDK for Python (okta-client-python) includes client authentication values (client_secret or JWT assertions) as query parameters in the front-channel authorization URL when executing the authorization code flow without Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR). When PAR is disabled, unsupported by the authorization server, or fails, the SDK falls back to standard authorization URL construction, transmitting these parameters via user-agent requests.
ERF file parser crash in 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19 allows denial of service
Tektronix K12xx file parser large loop in 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19 allows denial of service
Ascend file parser large loop in 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19 allows denial of service
PEAK CAN TRC file parser crash when built with older versions of GLib in 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 allows denial of service

Improper following of a certificate’s chain of trust in the remote-attestation verifier used to establish trust with Meta AI's confidential computing backend in WhatsApp for iOS before 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac Desktop before v2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before v2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android before v2.26.23.70 could have allowed someone positioned within Meta infrastructure to bypass the hardware root of trust by presenting clients with a VCEK certificate signed by a key other than the hardware manufacturer’s. Any such VCEK Cert would first have to be published to the third-party binary transparency ledger used by WhatsApp Private Processing. The ledger shows that every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, confirming no exploitation.

OceanWP WordPress Theme before 4.2.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the oceanwp_edd_terms_list() function in inc/edd/edd-helpers.php, which allows authenticated users with EDD download category creation permissions to inject malicious JavaScript by crafting a category name that breaks out of an unescaped HTML title attribute. Attackers can create a category name containing an event-handler payload that executes in the browser of visitors who interact with the category link on the public EDD archive page, potentially compromising an administrator's session if they view the affected page while authenticated.
A race condition was addressed with additional validation. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2. An app may be able to access sensitive user data.

The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires an administrator to approve the attacker's review, then export and re-import it using the plugin's default column mapping, with the import taking the INSERT branch — which occurs automatically on any site whose database table prefix is not the literal 'wp_', when the CSV has no comment_ID mapping, or when the original review has been trashed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Simply Schedule Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.13.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
